citeturn36search2 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 3 months ago; She prepares ballots, voting equipment, and voter lists, certifies nomination papers and initiative petitions, and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. ... The Town Clerk administers oaths of office and maintains appointments and resignations of all officials in Hawley.The Clerk bears the responsibility to ensure compliance with the State Open-Meeting Law and Conflict of Interest Law and to make sure that all public meetings of government entities are posted. ... Record Keeping The Town Clerk records and certifies all official actions of the town, including Town Meeting legislation and appropriations.

# Town Clerk

As the chief election official of a town and the keeper of permanent and vital records, the Town Clerk is the custodian of the past and a link to the future. The clerk works for, and reports to, the state and the residents of the town, not the Selectmen. While the duties of Town Clerks are largely defined by Massachusetts General Laws (MGL) and regulations, they vary slightly for each community.

### Record Keeping

The Town Clerk is the official custodian of Town Meeting votes and vital records dating back for two centuries. She records and certifies all official actions of the town and is the keeper of the town seal. The Town Clerk also performs genealogical research and is responsible for the town census.

### Elections

The Town Clerk serves as Chief Election Officer for the town. She is responsible for all elections and census work, as well as  voter registration and absentee ballots. She prepares ballots, voting equipment, and voter lists, certifies nomination papers and initiative petitions, and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. 
The Town Clerk acts as an Information Source about town departments and to the general public regarding all federal, state, and local regulations and town bylaws, rules, and regulations, as well as serving as Custodian of all Town Records. The Town Clerk can produce voter lists on demand. She also provides copies of the town bylaws, either digital or printed. The digital version is free; a printed copy costs $5.

### Records Access Officer

In compliance with the Massachusetts Records Law, Hawley has a Records Access Officer and an Alternate, and maintains a procedure whereby members of the public can gain access to public records.  Here is a guide to that process. The Records Access officer is our Town Clerk; her alternate is Gal Friday Tinky Weisblat. If you have questions about Records Access in Hawley, please use this email address (rao@townofhawley.com).

There is a $25 per hour fee for large search requests. Printed copies of Town Bylaws cost $5; digital copies are free. The Clerk charges 10 cents per page for copying records.

Hawley’s new valuation software includes a Public Access Database for property records, valuations, and the like.

Use the Database

#### Hawley’s Town Clerk, Elizabeth Van Iderstine

Ellie Van Iderstine is our Town Clerk. Ellie lives nearby and is passionate about local government. She is the former chair of the Hawlemont School Committee, and she has also worked part time for the Town of Williamsburg as the assistant to the Selectmen. Ellie holds office hours at the Hawley Town Office on Thursdays between 9 and 1. (These hours can vary; call her at 413-339-5518 before coming in.)

In the past,  the Town Clerk was an elected position eligible only to Hawley residents. No one has run ran for the position recently so in 2026 townspeople voted in 2026  to make Contact Ellie via email by clicking here (townclerk@townofhawley.com). Or call and leave a message for her at 413 339-5518.

Hawley, MA 01339-9621

  * 413 339-4959 fax

# News Flash

## *Hingham General News and Announcements*

Posted on: November 9, 2022

### [ARCHIVED] Election Results and Post Tabulation Announcement

Image: Town Seal Red on Gray 2 x 3

State Election Results for Hingham (PDF)

Town of Hingham Office of Town Clerk

In accordance with chapter 92 of the Acts of 2022, known as the VOTES Act, please be advised that the Town of Hingham will perform a post-election tabulation session for the November 8, 2022 State Election for ballots received on Election Day, November 8, 2022 after 1:00 PM and other ballots postmarked by November 8th returned by mail and received on or before 5:00 PM on November 12, 2022.  

This session will take place in Town Hall, the Central Meeting Room, 210 Central Street, Hingham, Massachusetts, beginning on Tuesday, November 15, 2022 at 9:00 AM and will be open to the public.

This notice is posted in Town Hall and on the Town Website.

Carol M. Falvey

# Holliston town election results include Select Board close call, Planning Board upset

Image

The Holliston town election was held on Tuesday, May 21. 

The Town Clerk’s unofficial results are listed below which include a Planning Board upset wherein the incumbent lost to another candidate. 

Candidates for Select Board included Damon D. Dimmick (1170 votes) and Tracey R. McSherry (1169 votes), Dimmick won by one vote. At press time, McSherry was gathering signatures to request a recount. 

Damon D. Dimmick won a Select Board seat by one vote. A recall is being requested. 

Select Board (3-year term) – Damon D. Dimmick 

Assessor of Taxes (3 yrs) – Jeffrey A. Marshall

Assessor of Taxes (2 yrs) – write-in candidate (unnamed at press time) 

School Committee (3 yrs), 3 seats – Hilary S. Bresnahan, Francis K. Ogura, Joseph M. Paru

Board of Health (3 yrs) – John D. Leary Jr.

School at 1401 Main Street in the Town of Holden.  At 6:00PM the Board of Selectmen and the newly 
elected Town Moderator, Joseph Sullivan, met to discuss and vote on reducing the quorum due to the 
State of Emergency as declared by the Governor of Massachusetts on March 10, 2020.  Holden Town 
Bylaws Article 1, Section 5 which states one percent of the registered voters of the Town shall constitute a 
quorum.  As of June 12th, the last day to register as a voter there were 14,100 registered voters requiring 
141 voters to be in attendance.  The Selectmen voted to reduce the quorum to a minimum of 25 
registered voters.  There was a quorum present of two hundred and seventy four (274) registered Holden 
voters and an additional twelve (12) guests. 
 
All non-voters or non-residents of the Town were asked to be recognized by the Moderator: 
 
Jeanne Survell, Town Clerk

## Members

  * Lisa M. Pedroli, Town Clerk

## Functions & Responsibilities

The Town Clerk is responsible for maintaining records for the Town and for being the general informant to inhabitants. Vital statistics, licenses, public notices, town meeting information, Zoning Board decisions, business certificates, raffle permits and fuel storage permits are all issued from this office. The Clerk works closely with the Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth as well as the Attorney General's Office.

Another chief function is elections. Voting lists, ballot preparation, certification of nomination papers and initiative petitions, voter registrations, annual census, resident book, list to the Office of the Jury Commissioner are all handled from this office.

The Town Clerk is elected for renewable three year terms and receives a salary.

ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION RESULTS  

May 9, 2023  

Hopedale, Massachusetts  

In accordance with the posted warrant, for Annual Town Election, the inhabitants of the Town of Hopedale, qualified to vote in elections met in the Draper Gymnasium at 7:00 am with Warden Ellen Murphy in charge of the election.

At 8:00 pm the polls were closed. The number of ballots agreed with the checklist, and it was announced that the number of ballots cast was eight hundred seventy (870) which was 20.65%. At the time of the election there were four thousand two hundred thirteen (4213) inhabitants registered to vote.

The early voting ballots were processed during the polling hours. There were thirty-nine (39) vote by mail applications and thirty (30) were returned. Eight hundred forty (840) residents voted at the polls on elections day.

A True Record, Attest:

Lisa M. Pedroli  
Hopedale Town Clerk

Town and establish interventions that will improve wellness. In 2022, 10 residents died from
COVID-19. Two residents of Hopkinton died of suicide and another two died from drug
overdoses.
Food Establishment Permitting and Inspections
All permanent food establishments are required to be permitted by the department, and must be
inspected, at a minimum, two times per year. Temporary food establishments, such as those
associated with the Boston Marathon, PolyArts Festival and the Farmers Market, are also
permitted and inspected.  Follow-up inspections occur when violations are noted, and to ensure
compliance with the Food Code including the food allergy notice requirements. The office
investigates all complaints received regarding food services or food products; a total of 19
complaint inspections were conducted. A total of 103 routine inspections were performed in
2022. We adopted a digital inspection system for food service, retail and housing inspections.  
Recreational Swimming and Camps for Children and Bathing Beaches
All swimming pools, camps and public beaches must be inspected and permitted by the agency
prior to use. A comprehensive camp inspection was conducted, and permits issued for the one
recreational camp for children that operated in the summer of 2022. During the swimming
season, the Department sampled the water at Sandy Beach on a weekly basis. The results of
this testing are reviewed by the Department and an annual report forwarded to the
Commonwealth of Massachusetts Department of Public Health.
 
Respectively submitted,
Dr. Richard Jacobs, Chairman
Nasiba Mannan, Vice Chairman
Regina Miloslavsky, Member
Shaun McAuliffe, Health Department Director
BOARD OF REGISTRARS
The Board of Registrars, as directed by the State and Federal Election Laws and the Secretary
of State, provides the opportunity for the voters of the Town of Hopkinton to have a voice in their
local government through participation in the democratic process. The Board of Registrars
ensures that all elections conducted by the Town are fair and transparent. The members of the
Board of Registrars are nominated by the Democratic and Republican Town Committees before
being appointed by the Select Board for three-year terms. Current members are Veda Kerr,
Doris Early, and Brian Karp. The Town Clerk also serves on the Board of Registrars as an
ex-officio full member. Board members assist with voter registration and cover extra registration
hours, as needed. Although, as in many communities, the day-to-day Board of Registrars’ duties
such as the running of elections, voter registrations, changes in voter status, and the annual
street listing count are performed by the Town Clerk’s office. The Registrars are instrumental in
conducting recounts and holding hearings on election related challenges and with the increased
scrutiny on the election process. The Registrars have seen increased duties in the conduct of
fair elections, ensure access, and investigation of potential fraud.

citeturn37search3 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 weeks ago; 2) Annual Town Election - second Tuesday in June from 7:00AM to 8:00PM - According to Chapter II, Section 1c of Hubbardston's General Bylaws, "That part of the Annual Town Meeting for the election of Town Officers and the determination of such matters as the laws that are required to be determined by ballot shall be held on the second Tuesday in June each year." ... Town Meeting warrants shall also be posted on the official Town of Hubbardston website and any official social media outlets at least fourteen (14) days prior to either a Special or Annual Town Meeting." ... You may register to vote in person at the Town Clerk’s Office during regular business hours, through the Registry of Motor Vehicles, through various other State Agencies, or by completing a mail-in registration affidavit and returning it to our office. ... If you move to another town or city in Massachusetts, you must re-register to vote in that community.

# Election/Town Meeting Information

All Elections and Town Meetings are held from 7:00am-8:00pm at the Hubbardston Center School Gym at 8 Elm Street (Hubbardston's polling location). Voter parking is located behind the gym, with entrance at 7 Main Street. 

## Elections/Town Meetings in Hubbardston during the year 2026:

1) Annual Town Meeting - According to Chapter II, Section 1c of Hubbardston's General Bylaws, "The part of the Annual Town Meeting for the conduct of business matters shall be held at 7:30 PM on the Monday of the week preceding the Annual Town Election or such other date prior to the end of the fiscal year as designated by the Select Board."
2) Annual Town Election - second Tuesday in June from 7:00AM to 8:00PM - According to Chapter II, Section 1c of Hubbardston's General Bylaws, "That part of the Annual Town Meeting for the election of Town Officers and the determination of such matters as the laws that are required to be determined by ballot shall be held on the second Tuesday in June each year."
3) State Primaries - Tuesday, September 1, 2026. Information on registration deadlines and voting by mail/early voting can be found here: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/recent-updates/upcoming-elections.htm

4) Special Town Meeting- Tuesday, October 27 at 7:00PM at Hubbardston Center School gym (more info below)

5) State Election - Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Information on registration deadlines and voting by mail/early voting can be found here: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/recent-updates/upcoming-elections.htm

Sample ballot for November 3, 2026 State Election can be found here: Sample State Election Ballot 2026
Massachusetts Voter Information can be found here: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/elections-and-voting.htm
Information on Registering to Vote can be found here: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/divisions/elections/voter-resources/registering-to-vote.htm

Information for Candidates:

  * Campaign Finance/Filing Requirements for Campaign Finance Reports - All candidates for municipal office, including all incumbent elected officials, are required to file 3 campaign finance reports. The first is due 8 days prior to the election, the second is due 30 days after the election, and the third is a year-end report due on January 20. The same requirements also apply to all active campaign/ballot question committees.  According to the campaign finance law, you must file a year-end report on Form CPF M102 with this office on or before January 20th. The reporting period covers the day after your last report through December 31 of the year of the election you ran in. If you did not receive any contributions, make any expenditures, or incur any liabilities during this reporting period, and you do not have a previous campaign balance, you have the option of signing an M102-0 affidavit form stating those facts. You may download the form online and send it to the Town Clerk, or come into the office to sign. Additional forms are available online through the Office of Campaign Finance if needed. Please call with any questions, or refer to Mass. General Law Chapter 55 for details on campaign finance law and associated penalties.

Any questions, please contact Melody Green, Town Clerk at townclerk@hubbardstonma.gov, stop in the office (located at 48 Gardner Road), or call 978-928-1400, extension 202.

## Dog Licensing

Dog licensing can be done by Mail: in person at the Hudson Town Clerk's office, or by dropping off a check or money order in the mail drop slot in front of Town Hall. Online payment is accepted as well.

## Town Clerk's Mission Statement

The Hull Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing competent, courteous, and efficient service to all residents and non-residents alike, also strives to work efficiently and cooperatively with all departments, boards and committees, as well as keeping the integrity of the office.

## General Powers & Duties

The Hull Town Clerk is elected by the registered voters of Hull. State law provides that the Town Clerk is the official keeper of the Town Seal and the Town's Oath Book. The Town Clerk, and members of his/her staff, also are Notaries Public and have the authority to notarize documents signed in their presence. The Town Clerk serves as the custodian of Town records and official documents. The Town Clerk is responsible for the maintenance, preservation and disposition of all Town records.

## Registrar of Vital Records & Statistics

The Town Clerk also acts as the Town Registrar of Vital Records and Statistics. The Town Clerk accepts for filing and maintains records of all births, deaths and marriages that occur in Hull. The Town Clerk is authorized to issue certified copies of birth, death and marriage records, and administers adoption and record-change depositions.

## Chief Election Official

The Town Clerk is the Chief Election Official and is authorized by state law to administer elections and election-related functions. In addition to the Town Clerk, the Town of Hull has three Registrars of Voters who are appointed by the Board of Selectmen, each serving a three-year term. The Registrars of Voters must always represent each of the two leading political parties. The daily administrations of election processes is managed by the Town Clerk.

## Mission Statement

The Lakeville Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing competent, courteous, and efficient service to all residents and non-residents alike, and also strives to work efficiently and cooperatively with all departments, boards, and committees, as well as keeping the integrity of the office.

## Responsibilities

  * The Lakeville Town Clerk serves the residents of Lakeville as the official custodian and record keeper of Town Meeting records and vital records dating from the present back to 1853. This office also performs genealogical research.
  * Is the chief election official, recording official, registrar of vital records (births, deaths, and marriages), as well as the public records official.
  * Issues state licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, business licenses (DDBAs and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, raffle/bazaar permits, and requests for public documents.
  * Is responsible for all elections, census and voter registration, nd absentee ballots, preparation of ballots, voting equipment, and voter lists, certification of nomination papers and initiative petitions, and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, as well as overseeing the polling place and the conduct of all election-related activity.

# Town Clerk

## Duties & Responsibilities

The Town Clerk's Office serves as the focal point of the Town Government. General information, direction, and assistance is provided to all citizens or others having business with the Town. The Town Clerk's Office is the municipal archival for the filing, maintenance, disposition, and preservation of most Town records and materials. The Town Clerk is responsible for all voter registration, election preparation, execution, and reporting of election results to the public and appropriate authorities.

## Services

  * Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed officials.
  * Conducts with the Board of Registrars 
    * Annual Town Census
    * Compiles Street, School Lists 
    * Election activities: including Voter Registration, Absentee & Early Voting.
  * Issues licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, burial permits, permits for raffles and bazaars, dog licenses, and fuel storage permits.
  * Posts meetings of all government bodies.
  * Records and certifies Planning and Zoning Board decisions.

# Board of Registrars

## Mission

The Board of Registrars oversees elections in the Town of Leicester.

## Duties

Massachusetts General Laws (MGL) Chapter 51 §15 requires that there shall be a Board of Registrars of Voters in every city or town other than one having a board of election commissioners or an election commission.

The Board of Registrars duties include:

  * Maintaining accurate lists of registered voters in the town
  * Conducting elections
  * Accepting nomination papers
  * Certifying initiative or referendum petitions.
  * Registering voters
  * Processing absentee voter applications
  * Processing address and party changes
  * Maintaining and testing voting equipment
  * Preparing and publishing lists of residents
  * Tallying election results
  * Hearing complaints of illegal or incorrect registration
  * Conducting election recounts

The Board also conducts an annual census and has other duties and responsibilities assigned to them under Chapter 51 of the Massachusetts General Laws.

# Town Clerk 

## Mission

Often considered the core of local government, the Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for local residents and citizens at large.

It is the mission of the Office of the Town Clerk to be a primary provider of information and quality services to the community and to work cooperatively and in coordination with the varied departments and groups while performing a myriad of tasks to achieve established goals and comply with state and local statutes.

The Leicester Town Clerk serves the residents of Leicester through its function as official record keeper for the Town Meeting and Vital Records and the Administration of Elections and voter related activities.

Records found in this office are: Birth, Marriage and Death Certificates; Zoning Decisions; Town Meeting Records; Annual Town Reports and Special Reports to Town Meeting; records of elections and lists of those who have served the Town of Leicester in elective or appointive office.

This office issues a number of licenses: Marriage licenses, Dog licenses, Business Certificates (D/B/A), Raffles and Bazaar permits.

# Board of Registrars

## Mission

The Board of Registrars oversees elections in the Town of Leicester.

## Duties

Massachusetts General Laws (MGL) Chapter 51 §15 requires that there shall be a Board of Registrars of Voters in every city or town other than one having a board of election commissioners or an election commission.

The Board of Registrars duties include:

  * Maintaining accurate lists of registered voters in the town
  * Conducting elections
  * Accepting nomination papers
  * Certifying initiative or referendum petitions.
  * Registering voters
  * Processing absentee voter applications
  * Processing address and party changes
  * Maintaining and testing voting equipment
  * Preparing and publishing lists of residents
  * Tallying election results
  * Hearing complaints of illegal or incorrect registration
  * Conducting election recounts

The Board also conducts an annual census and has other duties and responsibilities assigned to them under Chapter 51 of the Massachusetts General Laws.

# Town Clerk 

## Mission

Often considered the core of local government, the Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for local residents and citizens at large.

It is the mission of the Office of the Town Clerk to be a primary provider of information and quality services to the community and to work cooperatively and in coordination with the varied departments and groups while performing a myriad of tasks to achieve established goals and comply with state and local statutes.

The Leicester Town Clerk serves the residents of Leicester through its function as official record keeper for the Town Meeting and Vital Records and the Administration of Elections and voter related activities.

Records found in this office are: Birth, Marriage and Death Certificates; Zoning Decisions; Town Meeting Records; Annual Town Reports and Special Reports to Town Meeting; records of elections and lists of those who have served the Town of Leicester in elective or appointive office.

This office issues a number of licenses: Marriage licenses, Dog licenses, Business Certificates (D/B/A), Raffles and Bazaar permits.

## Duties

Image: Jacevote

Responsibilities of the Town Clerk's Office include (among other duties) running fair and honest elections, maintaining public records, public access officer, handling vital statistics, voter registration, short-term rental registration, dog licenses, and business certificates.

Below is the list of candidates for election at the upcoming Annual Town Election on May 11, 2026.

For those offices where there are no candidates, a write-in candidate can win the position with one vote, or one more vote than anyone else who has received any votes. If there is a tie, "failure to elect" is the result, and no one is elected. In the case of a failure to elect (either no write-ins or a tie) at the election then the Select Board is able to appoint someone to the board per MGL Chapter 41 Section 11.

# Town Clerk

## Responsibilities

### 
Roles

The Town Clerk acts as the Town's:

  * Chief Election Official
  * Recording Officer
  * Registrar of Vital Statistics

# Welcome to Leverett

Situated in western Massachusetts, Leverett is neighbor to the Five College area of Amherst, Hampshire, Smith, Mt. Holyoke and the University of Massachusetts.  Its diverse population of 2,000 is a rich mixture of teachers, students, farmers, lumbermen, gardeners, artists, professionals in the areas of medicine, law, and telecommunications.

Leverett is unusually rich in scenic beauty. Rattlesnake Gutter Road, in the heart of the town, is a two mile road through a glacial ravine, bordered by Brushy Mountain. The Sawmill River cascades over rocks in Moore’s Corner, before coming to the North Leverett millpond, and its picturesque historic mill. Leverett Pond, in the center of town, is a place of quiet beauty. The first Peace Pagoda in the U.S. sits majestically at the top of Cave Hill. Road names, such as Juggler Meadow, Teawaddle Hill, Cider Mill, Number Six, Rat Hollow, intrigue the traveler.

# Town Clerk

## Mission Statement

The Littleton Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing competent, courteous, and efficient service to all residents and non-residents alike, as well as, keeping the integrity of the Office.

## The Town Clerk's Office

  * Is the chief election official, recording official, registrar of vital records (births, deaths, and marriages), as well as, the public records official.
  * Issues state licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, business licenses (DBAs) and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, raffle/bazaar permits, and requests for public documents.
  * Is responsible for all elections, census and voter registration and absentee ballots, preparation of ballots, voting equipment and voter lists, certification of nomination papers and initiative petitions and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, as well as overseeing the polling place and the conduct of all elections and election related activity.

# City Clerk

As official record keeper for the City, the Clerk's Office files and maintains a series of records such as:

  * Board of Appeal and Planning Board Decisions
  * Business Certificates
  * Dog Licenses 
  * Municipal Ordinances and Minutes of All Boards and Commissions
  * Various Business Related Licenses
  * Vital Records (Births, Deaths, and Marriages)

As Clerk to the City Council, the office develops and distributes the Council agenda, keeps minutes of the meetings, provides notification of Council actions to affected parties and issues licenses on its behalf.

As the City's chief election officer, the City Clerk is responsible for all aspects of voter registration, absentee voting and election administration for all elections and serves as the Campaign Finance Officer for local elections. As licensing agent for the City, the office issues a variety of licenses and permits such as marriage licenses, auctioneer permits and raffle and bazaar permits.

## Respond to the City Census Online

## Due to high demand, the City Clerk's Office researches and responds to requests for genealogy on Wednesdays. Genealogical requests are considered requests for any vital records dated before 1920.

# City Clerk

As official record keeper for the City, the Clerk's Office files and maintains a series of records such as:

  * Board of Appeal and Planning Board Decisions
  * Business Certificates
  * Dog Licenses 
  * Municipal Ordinances and Minutes of All Boards and Commissions
  * Various Business Related Licenses
  * Vital Records (Births, Deaths, and Marriages)

As Clerk to the City Council, the office develops and distributes the Council agenda, keeps minutes of the meetings, provides notification of Council actions to affected parties and issues licenses on its behalf.

As the City's chief election officer, the City Clerk is responsible for all aspects of voter registration, absentee voting and election administration for all elections and serves as the Campaign Finance Officer for local elections. As licensing agent for the City, the office issues a variety of licenses and permits such as marriage licenses, auctioneer permits and raffle and bazaar permits.

## Respond to the City Census Online

## Due to high demand, the City Clerk's Office researches and responds to requests for genealogy on Wednesdays. Genealogical requests are considered requests for any vital records dated before 1920.

## Forms

  * File a Claim

Town Clerk | New Marlborough, MA (https://newmarlboroughma.gov/1208/Town-Clerk) citeturn55search0 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: last month; The Town Clerk is the official record keeper for the Town of New Marlborough.The Town Clerk's Office also handles annual Town census, voter registration, elections and issues licenses and certificates as described below. # Town Clerk Welcome to the Town Clerk's Office website. We hope you find the following information helpful and informative concerning the services we provide to the residents of New Marlborough. The Town Clerk is the official record keeper for the Town of New Marlborough. The Town Clerk's Office also handles annual Town census, voter registration, elections and issues licenses and certificates as described below. ## Services offered by the Town Clerk's Office include the following: * Business Certificate (dba) * Notarization of documents * Payment of non-criminal complaint violations * Posting meetings for all municipal boards and committees * Vital Statistics - births, marriages and death certificates * Voter Registration * Town Calendar * Town Meeting minutes ## The following licenses can be obtained from the Town Clerk's Office: * Dog Licenses * Marriage License ## The following documents may be obtained from the Town Clerk's Office: * Board of Appeals filing application * By-Laws * Protective By-Laws ## Staff * Katherine Chretien, CMMC, CMC, Town Clerk, Notary, Public Records Officer Term Expires: June 30, 2029 * Jennifer Greenberg, Assistant Town Clerk ## Board of Registrars * Katherine Chretien Term Expires: June 30, 2027 * Sharon Fleck Term Expires: June 30, 2027 * Ramona Bauer Term Expires: June 30, 2027 * Vacancy: 1 ### Contact Us 1. #### Katherine Chretien CMMC, CMC, Town Clerk, Notary, Public Records Officer Email Kathy Chretien (KChretien@newmarlboroughma.gov) 2. #### Town Clerk Physical Address 807 Mill River Southfield Rd. # Election Information

## Election Information

#### WHERE DO I VOTE?                                         

2026 Election Schedule

## You may check your voter registration status online here: Voter Registrations

Mail-In Voter Registration Form The last day, and hour, to register to vote for the State Election is October 24, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. at the Town Clerk's Office. 
Online Voter RegistrationVoter Registration Status

## Election Day Polling Locations

Precincts 1 and 2 vote at the Active Living Center. Precincts 3 and 4 vote at Town Hall. Precinct 5 vote at the Mashpee Public Library. If you do not know your precinct please use the 'Where Do I Vote" link listed above.

## Preparing for the November 3, 2026 Election

The November 3, 2026 ballot is a multi-page ballot. There are 15 offices, 1 local ballot question (Question A), and 9 statewide ballot questions on the ballot.

You must apply annually to receive a ballot by mail. 

Vote By Mail is available for the November 3, 2026 State Election. The deadline to submit a Vote By Mail by 5:00pm five days prior to an election (October 27, 2026); we recommend submitting your application as soon as possible to ensure you receive your ballot in time. The US Postal Service recommends allowing up to 7 days for mail delivery. 

2026 Vote By Mail Application BALLOTS DO NOT GET FORWARDED; please put a direct mailing address on the application (This application requires a handwritten signature)
If you have submitted a Vote By Mail Application you can track your ballot using the following link: Track My Ballot
Absentee Ballot Application

## Deadline to Receive Vote By Mail Ballots for November 3, 2026 State Election:

In-Person or Drop Box: All Vote By Mail ballots must be returned to the Town Clerk's office or placed in the secure drop box located at the front entrance of Town Hall no later than 8:00PM on November 3, 2026. PLEASE NOTE: Ballots cannot be dropped off at a polling place on Election Day.

By Mail: Vote by Mail ballots returned by mail must be postmarked by November 3, 2026 and received by the office no later than 5:00PM on November 6, 2026 in order to be counted. 

IMPORTANT: If you are mailing your ballot on Election Day, we strongly recommended to hand delivering it to a Post Office counter and request a postmark. Ballots deposited in a mailbox or postal drop box may not receive a postmark on the same day and may not be received intime to be counted.

## About

The Election Commission is responsible for managing and supervising elections, the annual census, and registering voters in the City of Medford, while ensuring compliance with the federal, state and local election laws, policies, and guidelines established by the Massachusetts General Laws and the City of Medford ordinances and municipal code.

General Information – The information listed below is for reference, if you have further questions, please call or email the Election Commission office - elections@medford-ma.gov or call the office at 781-393-2491.

## Early Voting Information

In person early voting for the November 3 General Election will be held from Saturday, October 17 through Friday, October 30 in City Hall Chambers, on the 2nd floor of Medford City Hall Medford City Hall.
If you have moved, you can update your registration by filling out a new voter registration form (PDF) and returning it to the Election Commission Office or by making the change online.

## Voter Registration

Voter registration options include:

  * Online via www.sec.state.ma.us/ele/eleidx.htm 
  * Visiting the Elections Commission Office at Medford City Hall, Room 102.

  * Requesting a voter registration card via email elections@medford-ma.gov
  * Requesting a voter registration card to be mailed, by calling 781-393-2490. 

Please be aware the voter registration deadlines still apply.

In addition, branches of the state Registry of Motor Vehicles, social service agencies and military recruitment offices provide voter registration services.

## Accessibility Resources for Voters

  * Information for Voters 
  * Accessible Vote by Mail application link (state.ma.us)
  * Please contact the Election Commission Office ahead of the election if you have questions about accommodation and accessibility. Several handicap accessible parking spots will be available at the different polling locations. The accessible voting machine, the AutoMARK is available for use by any registered voter. This machine can read the ballot to you through headphones, magnifying the ballot text, in addition it will mark the ballot for you. Election workers are limited in the assistance they can provide voters using this machine; however, voters may bring and assign someone to assist them. Handheld magnifiers and lights can be requested at the check-in tables. Please do not hesitate to ask an election worker if you need any assistance.

# Election Results: General Election, Nov. 4, 2025

City News Posted on November 04, 2025 | Last Updated on December 08, 2025

The Melrose City Clerk has shared the following official, certified results of the November 4, 2025 General Election. 

The ballot included a Proposition 2 1/2 override referendum, all eleven City Council seats (four at-large and seven by ward), and three at-large School Committee seats. Sample ballots are available here.

In total, 11,227 Melrose voters cast a vote in the General Election, representing approximately 52% of all registered voters in the City. The results are summarized in the tables below and available in a PDF document here.

## Ballot Questions

### Questions 1A, 1B and 1C are separate questions. You may vote for or against each question independently. Each question requires a majority of those voting on that question to pass. If more than one question passes, the question with the highest dollar amount will prevail.

> 1A. Shall the City of Melrose be allowed to assess an additional $13,500,000 in real estate and personal property taxes for the purposes of funding: 17 school, 5 public works, and 2 police officer positions (salaries and benefits); city and school employee union contracts and benefits; school technology and curriculum needs; public works, senior center, veterans services, and library programs; and repairs and maintenance to roads, sidewalks, buildings, and parks for which the monies from this assessment will be used for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025?

# Town Clerk

The Merrimac Town Clerk’s Office is committed to providing the general public with essential documents and day-to-day services. The Town Clerk’s office is dedicated to the preservation of the Town’s official and vital records and statistics. Among other duties, the Town Clerk records and certifies all votes passed at Town Meeting, administers and records oaths of office to town officials and records various instruments as required by law. The Town Clerk also issues certificates and licenses, prepares street and voting lists and supervises all elections.

Doing Business As (DBA)

### Certificates

Business Certificates must be filed by an unincorporated business located in Merrimac that is operating under a name other than one’s own, such as, Helen Good DBA Good Cards and Gifts. The fee for a Business Certificate is $25 and the certificate is valid for 4 years. Certificates must be renewed every 4 years if the business remains in operation.

# Town Clerk

The Merrimac Town Clerk’s Office is committed to providing the general public with essential documents and day-to-day services. The Town Clerk’s office is dedicated to the preservation of the Town’s official and vital records and statistics. Among other duties, the Town Clerk records and certifies all votes passed at Town Meeting, administers and records oaths of office to town officials and records various instruments as required by law. The Town Clerk also issues certificates and licenses, prepares street and voting lists and supervises all elections.

Doing Business As (DBA)

### Certificates

Business Certificates must be filed by an unincorporated business located in Merrimac that is operating under a name other than one’s own, such as, Helen Good DBA Good Cards and Gifts. The fee for a Business Certificate is $25 and the certificate is valid for 4 years. Certificates must be renewed every 4 years if the business remains in operation.

## Overview

The town clerk is the chief record-keeper, registrar, and election officer for a municipality. They manage vital records, coordinate local elections, license essential activities and safeguard public documents.

The core functions of a town clerk include:

  * Elections and Voter Registration: Serves as the chief election officer. They oversee voter registration, maintain voting lists, process absentee ballots, conduct local and state elections, and certify results.
  * Vital Records: Records and preserves official births, deaths, and marriages that happen in the community. They issue certified copies of these records and marriage licenses.
  * Public Records and Governance: Acts as custodian of the municipal seal. They maintain town meeting minutes, ordinances, and bylaws, ensuring the public has compliant access to these records under state laws. They also administer the oath of office to newly elected or appointed local officials.

# Town Clerk

Assistant Town Clerk:  Mark Doane
Elected  for three-year term
Assistant appointed by Town Clerk

## Overview

The town clerk is the chief record-keeper, registrar, and election officer for a municipality. They manage vital records, coordinate local elections, license essential activities and safeguard public documents.

The core functions of a town clerk include:

  * Elections and Voter Registration: Serves as the chief election officer. They oversee voter registration, maintain voting lists, process absentee ballots, conduct local and state elections, and certify results.
  * Vital Records: Records and preserves official births, deaths, and marriages that happen in the community. They issue certified copies of these records and marriage licenses.
  * Public Records and Governance: Acts as custodian of the municipal seal. They maintain town meeting minutes, ordinances, and bylaws, ensuring the public has compliant access to these records under state laws. They also administer the oath of office to newly elected or appointed local officials.

This office also prepares and oversees all Town and State Elections held here in Milford and the election results. In addition, we also maintain the Annual Street Listing/Town Census, Town Meeting minutes, and voter registration records. The Town Clerk's Office is also responsible for posting all meeting notices and registering DBA certificates, dog licenses, physical registrations and much more. ## Genealogical Research The Town Clerk's Office has Vital Records (Births, Deaths, Marriages) dating back to the 1800's. Please send an email request to the Town Clerk (townclerksoffice@townofmilford.com) that includes the names and dates you wish to be researched. ### Quick Links 1. Monthly Newsletters 2. The last day to register to vote for an election is 10 days before the date of the election. The Town Clerk’s office will be open until 8 pm  You many register to vote as long as you will turn 18 years of age on or prior to the date of the election. What hours are the polls are open? For the Town Election the polls are open at 7 am and close at 8 pm in the evening. For all State Election the polls will open at 7 am in the morning and close at 8 pm in the evening.  Anyone in line when the polls close will be able to vote. How can I get an absentee ballot? You may get an application for an absentee ballot in the Town Clerk’s office or you may download the application here. Election Results September 6, 2022-Official Results (PDF) ## Returning your Ballot There are several options for returning your ballot. You may return your ballot by: * Mailing it back to your local election office * Hand-delivering your ballot to your local election office; or * Dropping your ballot off at an early voting location during early voting hours; or * Using a ballot drop box provided by your town. Ballots cannot be dropped off at a polling place on Election Day. Your ballot must reach the Milford Town Clerk's Office by 8 p.m. on Election Day in order to be counted. Ballots that arrive after that time – even if they are postmarked on or before Election Day – will not be counted.  For General Elections, ballots returned in person or by drop box must reach your local election office by 8 p.m. on Election Day. Ballots returned by mail from inside the United States must reach your local election office by 5 p.m. on the third day following the election and can only be counted if they are postmarked by Election Day.  ### Quick Links 1. # Town Clerk

### Responsibilities and Services

  * Conducts the annual town census.
  * Oversees and conducts all elections and maintains voter registration records.
  * Administers campaign finance laws.
  * Issues certain permits and business certificates.
  * Issues dog and kennel licenses.
  * Records and preserves birth, marriage, and death records.
  * Provides certified copies of vital records.
  * Records and certifies official actions of town government.
  * Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed members of local boards and committees.
  * Records Access Officer for all Public Records Requests
  * Burial Agent
  * Registrar
  * State Ethics Liaison

# Town Clerk

### Responsibilities and Services

  * Conducts the annual town census.
  * Oversees and conducts all elections and maintains voter registration records.
  * Administers campaign finance laws.
  * Issues certain permits and business certificates.
  * Issues dog and kennel licenses.
  * Records and preserves birth, marriage, and death records.
  * Provides certified copies of vital records.
  * Records and certifies official actions of town government.
  * Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed members of local boards and committees.
  * Records Access Officer for all Public Records Requests
  * Burial Agent
  * Registrar
  * State Ethics Liaison

# Town Clerk

## Overview

The Office of the Town Clerk is the core of local government and serves as a principal point of contact for local residents and citizens at large. During the course of the regular business, the Town Clerk is in contact with every level of government. This includes state agencies, county government and almost every officer and board or committee in the Town of Milton. It is the mission of this office to maintain the following: constantly improve the administration within the restraints of the applicable laws through sound management and financial practices; to maintain standards of quality and integrity; to be mindful of neutrality and impartiality; to render equal services to all by extending the same treatment we wish to receive ourselves; and to conduct the matters of this office above reproach and to merit public confidence in our community.

Please be advised the Office of the Town Clerk is closed to the public during the hours of 1:00PM -2:00PM

## Annual Town Census 2026

The Annual Town Census was mailed on January 6, 2026.  Please confirm/update your census form, sign and return to the Office of the Town Clerk within ten days of its receipt.  Failure to do this could result in voter status becoming inactive.

Montague is a diverse area that is rich in history and culture that includes more than 10,000 years of early Native American habitation, as well as the Colonial and Industrial history that is embodied in the National Historic Register Districts of Montague Center and Turners Falls – a planned industrial community.

The Town’s landscape, 31.5 square miles, is a rare combination of rolling hills, fertile farmlands, historic mills and residential villages. It is a thriving town of 8,580 people that offers a unique mixture of business and industrial opportunities, easily accessible to Route 2 and Interstate 91. Montague is also perfectly situated among New England’s finest skiing, canoeing, hiking and biking opportunities, including the Turners Falls Bikeway.

The Town prides itself on a lively arts community and convenient access to the cultural resources of the “Five College Area”. # Elections & Voting

This page provides information on upcoming elections, how to register to vote, update registration details, and check registration status, ensuring residents are prepared for upcoming elections.

## Voting In Person

  * Election Day: Nantucket High School, 10 Surfside Road. Polls will be open from 7 am to 8 pm on election day.
  * In-Person Early Voting - State Elections ONLY: Town Hall, 16 Broad Street. Hours will be posted online and in the local newspaper.
  * In-Person Absentee Voting – State & Local Elections. For persons who will be out of town on Election Day: you may cast an absentee ballot in person at the Town Clerk’s Office until 12 p.m. on the day before the election. (If the day before the election is a weekend or holiday, in-person absentee voting will end at 5 p.m. on the last business day before the election).

## Voting By Mail

Vote By ballots may be requested by any registered voter of the Town of Nantucket, and a reason is not required. You may apply for a vote-by-mail ballot at the Town Clerk’s Office or through the Secretary of State’s website. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Town and County Clerk’s Office serves as a vital connection between the public and local government.

The census is a requirement of Massachusetts General Law, and it is important that all residents return them to the Town Clerk’s office promptly.   Failure to respond to the census will result in removal from the active voting list and may result in removal registration rolls.   Residents should not use the census form for the purpose of voter registration. Any resident who is not registered  to vote may register at the Town Clerk’s office or by mailing a voter registration form to the Town Cler’s office.   Parents of college students or members of the military who are registered to vote in New Ashford should be aware that by deleting them from the census form will remove them from the active voters list.   Also, households that have dependent children in them, but that are not listed on the census form should add their children to the form and complete the information that pertains to each child. Parents of college students or members of the military who are registered to vote in New Ashford should be aware that by deleting them from the census form will remove them from the active voters list. # New Ashford CENSUS Info 01/16/2026Documents TOWN OF NEW ASHFORD Susan  Supranowicz, Town Clerk 188 Mallery Road New Ashford, Ma. 01237 Phone (414) 458-5461 cell (413) 217-4342 The New Ashford 2026 Annual Street listing will be mailed to all New Ashford residents this week. The census is a requirement of Massachusetts General Law, and it is important that all residents return them to the Town Clerk’s office promptly.   Failure to respond to the census will result in removal from the active voting list and may result in removal registration rolls.   Residents should not use the census form for the purpose of voter registration. Any resident who is not registered  to vote may register at the Town Clerk’s office or by mailing a voter registration form to the Town Cler’s office.   Parents of college students or members of the military who are registered to vote in New Ashford should be aware that by deleting them from the census form will remove them from the active voters list.   Also, households that have dependent children in them, but that are not listed on the census form should add their children to the form and complete the information that pertains to each child. Information regarding the children is not a public record and is used only by the schools for enrollment purposes.   All forms should be returned either by mail or can be dropped in the blue locked box outside of the town hall.   Anyone that did not receive a census form in the mail or have any questions pertaining to the form should contact the Town Clerk at the Town Hall, call Town Hall, call my cell phone or contact  the town clerk at email townclerk@newashford-ma.us.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026 TOWN OF NEW ASHFORD IMPORTANT DATES – Town of New Ashford (https://www.newashford-ma.us/2026-town-of-new-ashford-important-dates/) citeturn128search2 [wordlim: 200] Published: 9 months ago; Crawled: 3 weeks ago; # 2026 TOWN OF NEW ASHFORD IMPORTANT DATES01/16/2026 Town Clerk2026 TOWN OF NEW ASHFORD IMPORTANT DATES ... ### This guide outlines multiple options to voters to participate in the fall 2026 elections.

### Vote by Mail, Vote Early in Person or Vote on Election Day

### VOTE BY MAIL APPLICATION DEADLINE

 State Primary Election  |  September 1, 2026  | Pct. 1: 3 Morgan Ave.Pct. 2: 1 Lunt St. (Library)   | 7 AM – 8 PM  |  August 22, 2026  |  August 25^{th} – 5 PM
 State Election  |  November 3, 2026  | Pct 1: 3 Morgan Ave.Pct. 2: 1 Lunt st. (Library)  | 7 AM – 8 PM  |  October 24, 2026  |  October 27^{th} – 5PM

 

### *ONLINE MAIL-IN BALLOT APPLICATION SYSTEM:

Voters who are prepared to apply for September (see Primary selection of ballots below) and the November elections may apply utilizing the Online Mail-In Ballot Application System.

### SELECTION OF BALLOT TYPES – (PRIMARY ELECTIONS ONLY)

  * In a primary election, a voter who is NOT registered in a political party must choose a ballot type on the application to vote by mail or in person voting (early or on election day).
  * We are unable to process applications for Unenrolled (commonly known as Independent) voters who do not select a party ballot type on their application.
  * Unenrolled voters who select a party ballot type do no become registered in that party – they remain Unenrolled/Independent voters.
  * Voters who are registered in one of the 2 political parties (Democratic or Republican) MUST take that party ballot and are not given a choice of party ballot type.

 

### VOTE EARLY IN PERSON

Early Voting in person will be available for the fall 2026 elections.

An application is not required to vote early in person…just show up and vote!

 

### State Primary Election Early Voting in Person

Period:   Saturday, August 22^{nd} 7:00 AM - 1:00 PM & Monday, August 24 thru August 27 8:00 AM - 4:00 PM

Location:  Town Offices – 12 Kent Way – Suite 101 – Town Clerk’s Office

### VOTE BY MAIL APPLICATION DEADLINE

 State Primary Election  |  September 1, 2026  | Pct. 1: 3 Morgan Ave.Pct. 2: 1 Lunt St. (Library)   | 7 AM – 8 PM  |  August 22, 2026  |  August 25^{th} – 5 PM
 State Election  |  November 3, 2026  | Pct 1: 3 Morgan Ave.Pct. 2: 1 Lunt st. (Library)  | 7 AM – 8 PM  |  October 24, 2026  |  October 27^{th} – 5PM

 

### *ONLINE MAIL-IN BALLOT APPLICATION SYSTEM:

Voters who are prepared to apply for September (see Primary selection of ballots below) and the November elections may apply utilizing the Online Mail-In Ballot Application System.

### SELECTION OF BALLOT TYPES – (PRIMARY ELECTIONS ONLY)

  * In a primary election, a voter who is NOT registered in a political party must choose a ballot type on the application to vote by mail or in person voting (early or on election day).
  * We are unable to process applications for Unenrolled (commonly known as Independent) voters who do not select a party ballot type on their application.
  * Unenrolled voters who select a party ballot type do no become registered in that party – they remain Unenrolled/Independent voters.
  * Voters who are registered in one of the 2 political parties (Democratic or Republican) MUST take that party ballot and are not given a choice of party ballot type.

 

### VOTE EARLY IN PERSON

Early Voting in person will be available for the fall 2026 elections.

An application is not required to vote early in person…just show up and vote!

# Town Clerk

Welcome to the Town Clerk's Office website! We hope that you find the following information helpful and informative concerning the services that we provide to the residents of North Andover.

## Business Certificates (DBA’s, Doing Business As)

Find more information on how to obtain a Business Certificate. 

## Dog Licensing

  * Those residents who have access to a computer can license their Dog(s) online. By Mail: North Andover Town Clerk, 120 Main Street, North Andover, MA 01845, Or drop off check in the black Town Hall Business Mail drop box in front of Town Hall.
  * Please be aware that dogs have to be current with their rabies vaccination(s), please send with registration.
  * Standard License Fees 1-Year
Unaltered Dog $20
Spayed/Neutered Dog $19
  * Effective January 1, 2021, any dog owner age 70 + can now register their dog at no cost.  Please contact the Town Clerk's office.  Proof of age will be required.
  * View a listing of current registered dogs

## Elections

  * Click here to submit a vote by mail application.  If you are not able to print out the application, please send any written form of correspondence with your signature requesting an absentee ballot.  NOTE:  An application must be submitted for each calendar year.  Applications from prior year(s) do not carry over.
  * Absentee ballots are available by contacting the Town Clerk's office at 978-688-9501.  Absentee ballots are by appointment only.
  * These requests should be emailed to the Town Clerk (vote@northandoverma.gov), mailed to: North Andover Town Clerk, 120 Main Street or placed in the Town Hall Business Mail Dropbox in front of Town Hall.

Marriage Intentions / Justice of the Peace Services

  * Please call the office at 978-688-9501 to schedule an appointment to file for a marriage license.  If you are in need of a Justice of the Peace to perform your wedding vows, please email the Town Clerk / JP, Dawne Warren (dwarren@northandoverma.gov).  Learn how to obtain a marriage license.

## Vital Records Request

If you wish to request a birth, marriage or death record, please click below.  The event must have occurred in North Andover in order for us to have the record in our files.  Feel free to call to confirm before processing the online request.

# Town Clerk

Welcome to the Town Clerk's Office website! We hope that you find the following information helpful and informative concerning the services that we provide to the residents of North Andover.

## Business Certificates (DBA’s, Doing Business As)

Find more information on how to obtain a Business Certificate. 

## Dog Licensing

  * Those residents who have access to a computer can license their Dog(s) online. By Mail: North Andover Town Clerk, 120 Main Street, North Andover, MA 01845, Or drop off check in the black Town Hall Business Mail drop box in front of Town Hall.
  * Please be aware that dogs have to be current with their rabies vaccination(s), please send with registration.
  * Standard License Fees 1-Year
Unaltered Dog $20
Spayed/Neutered Dog $19
  * Effective January 1, 2021, any dog owner age 70 + can now register their dog at no cost.  Please contact the Town Clerk's office.  Proof of age will be required.
  * View a listing of current registered dogs

## Elections

  * Click here to submit a vote by mail application.  If you are not able to print out the application, please send any written form of correspondence with your signature requesting an absentee ballot.  NOTE:  An application must be submitted for each calendar year.  Applications from prior year(s) do not carry over.
  * Absentee ballots are available by contacting the Town Clerk's office at 978-688-9501.  Absentee ballots are by appointment only.
  * These requests should be emailed to the Town Clerk (vote@northandoverma.gov), mailed to: North Andover Town Clerk, 120 Main Street or placed in the Town Hall Business Mail Dropbox in front of Town Hall.

Marriage Intentions / Justice of the Peace Services

  * Please call the office at 978-688-9501 to schedule an appointment to file for a marriage license.  If you are in need of a Justice of the Peace to perform your wedding vows, please email the Town Clerk / JP, Dawne Warren (dwarren@northandoverma.gov).  Learn how to obtain a marriage license.

## Vital Records Request

If you wish to request a birth, marriage or death record, please click below.  The event must have occurred in North Andover in order for us to have the record in our files.  Feel free to call to confirm before processing the online request.

# Town Clerk

Contact the Town Clerk

Online Payment Center

Order Birth, Marriage, Death Certificates; Pay for Dog Licenses, Late Fees; Order Documents
Office Hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday 8:30 am to 2 pm, Tuesday Evenings 5 pm to 7 pm, Wednesday 8:30 am to 12 pm

The Town Clerk is elected every three years. The Town Clerk is:

  * Chief Election Official: Oversees all elections, voter registration sessions, certifies nomination papers, initiative petitions and conducts annual town census
  * Recording Officer: Records, certifies and maintains all official actions of the town
  * Registry of Vital Statistics: Registers all birth, marriage, and death records occurring within the community
  * Public Records Officer: Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed members. Posts all meetings of government bodies. Provides certified copies of vital records.Maintains records of all local bylaws
  * Licensing Officer: Issues licenses and permits: marriage, dog, and permits for raffles and bazaars
  * Public Information Officer: Responds to inquiries from the general public on information available through the officer

## ALL ELECTIONS ARE HELD AT 29 FOREST ST., SENIOR CENTER

Annual Town Election: Held the first Monday of May from 7 am to 8 pm at the Senior Center located at 29 Forest Street.
Annual Town Meeting: Held the second Friday of June at 7:30 pm in the Elementary School Auditorium.

# Town Clerk

Online Payment Center

Order Birth, Marriage, Death Certificates; Pay for Dog Licenses, Late Fees; Order Documents
Office Hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday 8:30 am to 2 pm, Tuesday Evenings 5 pm to 7 pm, Wednesday 8:30 am to 12 pm

The Town Clerk is elected every three years. The Town Clerk is:

  * Chief Election Official: Oversees all elections, voter registration sessions, certifies nomination papers, initiative petitions and conducts annual town census
  * Recording Officer: Records, certifies and maintains all official actions of the town
  * Registry of Vital Statistics: Registers all birth, marriage, and death records occurring within the community
  * Public Records Officer: Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed members. Posts all meetings of government bodies. Provides certified copies of vital records.Maintains records of all local bylaws
  * Licensing Officer: Issues licenses and permits: marriage, dog, and permits for raffles and bazaars
  * Public Information Officer: Responds to inquiries from the general public on information available through the officer

## ALL ELECTIONS ARE HELD AT 29 FOREST ST., SENIOR CENTER

Annual Town Election: Held the first Monday of May from 7 am to 8 pm at the Senior Center located at 29 Forest Street.
Annual Town Meeting: Held the second Friday of June at 7:30 pm in the Elementary School Auditorium.

## Description

Often considered the doorway to local government, the Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for residents and visitors alike. The Town Clerk is the chief election official, recording official, registrar of vital records, public records official, and licensing officer. The Town Clerk oversees the polling places and the conduct of all elections and election-related activity, and records all actions of Town Meeting. The Clerk's Office maintains the municipal code, the official Town bulletin board, oaths of office, appointments and resignations of all Town Officials. The Clerk's Office issues state licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, business licenses and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, raffle/bazaar permits and certified requests for public documents. This office responds to inquiries from the public as well as from other departments, boards and committees.

## Mission

It is the mission of this office to be a reliable provider of information and quality services to the community and its residents, and to work cooperatively and in concert with all departments, boards and committees while complying with state and local statutes.

In Northfield, the Town Clerk serves as the Town's Campaign and Political Finance Director for all local campaigns.As a result, the financial disclosure statements of candidate and ballot question committees must be filed with the Town Clerk and maintained for public inspection. # Elections ## Sample Ballot November 3, 2026 1. Northfield November 3 2026 Sample Ballot Voting Schedule for remaining elections: * Northfield Special  Election (Day of): Tuesday October 6, 2026 from noon to 8 pm * State Election (Early Voting) : Saturday, October 24 thru Friday, October 30 (Hours below) * State Election (Day of): Tuesday, November 3 from 7am to 8 pm ## Early Voting Hours for November 3rd Election  Saturday October 17- 9am to 1pm Monday October 19- 9am to 4pm Tuesday October 20- 9am to 4pm Wednesday October 21- 9am to 4pm Thursday October 22- 9am to 4pm Saturday October 24- 8am to noon Monday October 26- 9am to 4pm Tuesday October 27- 9am to pm Wednesday October 28- 9am to 4pm Thursday October 29- 9am to 4pm Friday October 30- 9am to noon ## ## Northfield Voting Location Voting for all elections in the Town of Northfield take place at the Town Hall, located at 69 Main Street. The Town Clerk is authorized by state law to administer elections and elections-related processes and functions. There also are three Registrars of Voters who are appointed by the Board of Selectmen, each serving a three-year term. The Town Clerk administers the day-to-day process for elections. 1. Sample Ballots 1. Voting in Northfield Poll Location:  Northfield Town Hall 69 Main Street The hours of polling for each election will be posted on the Town's website and announced in the newspapers. When you approach the check-in table, first tell the poll worker the name of the street where you live, then the number of your residence and finally your name. As the voters list is arranged by street, this is the quickest way to receive your ballot and keep any lines moving. In a primary election, voters who are registered in a political party may only obtain a ballot for that party. If you are an "unenrolled voter" (commonly referred to as an "independent voter"), you may request the ballot of any party participating in the primary election. If your name does not appear on the list of voters, the poll worker will contact the Town Clerk to determine if your voter status. The Northfield Town Clerk conducts all presidential primaries, state primaries, and state and presidential elections. The Town Clerk also conducts the Annual Town Election. The responsibilities of the Town Clerk include: voter registration; supplying nomination papers for candidates, initiatives and referenda; certification of signatures on all nomination papers and petitions; printing ballots for Town elections; maintenance of elections equipment; supervision of poll workers; tallying elections results; and maintaining and preserving the records of the election. 1. List of Voters The Town Clerk maintains the voters roll for Northfield. The Town Clerk endeavors to maintain as accurate a list as possible for use at the polls on Election Day. Voters are removed from the voters list because of death or a move outside of the Town and voters are added to the list as they register. In addition, all voters who change party affiliation are processed by the Town Clerk. 1. The Annual Municipal Census The Town Clerk conducts the annual census of Northfield’s households and publishes the results in a printed residents’ list (commonly known as the "Street List"). The publication contains an alphabetical-numerical list of all residents seventeen and older. The Town Clerk also prepares a non-public list of persons age three and older for the Pioneer Regional School District. 1. Nomination & Petition Papers The first step to running for office or placing a question on the ballot is to gather the required number of signatures of registered voters on petition papers. (A person may not have to complete nomination papers if he/she is nominated through the Town Caucus Process.  Please see the Town Clerk for specific details.)  The number of signatures depends on the office or the type of question. The Town Clerk supplies the petition papers. Candidates or question proponents must gather the required number of signatures on the petition papers supplied by the Town Clerk. Once the signatures are gathered, the petition papers are submitted to the Town Clerk for certification. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The 313th ANNUAL REPORT OF THE TOWN OF NORTON (https://www.nortonma.org/home/files/2024-213th-annual-town-report) citeturn62search13 [wordlim: 200] Published: 8 months ago; OFFICIAL RESULTS ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION | | | | | | ... If your name does not appear on the list of voters, the poll worker will contact the Town Clerk to determine if your voter status. The Northfield Town Clerk conducts all presidential primaries, state primaries, and state and presidential elections. The Town Clerk also conducts the Annual Town Election. The responsibilities of the Town Clerk include: voter registration; supplying nomination papers for candidates, initiatives and referenda; certification of signatures on all nomination papers and petitions; printing ballots for Town elections; maintenance of elections equipment; supervision of poll workers; tallying elections results; and maintaining and preserving the records of the election. 1. List of Voters The Town Clerk maintains the voters roll for Northfield. The Town Clerk endeavors to maintain as accurate a list as possible for use at the polls on Election Day. Voters are removed from the voters list because of death or a move outside of the Town and voters are added to the list as they register. In addition, all voters who change party affiliation are processed by the Town Clerk. 1. The Annual Municipal Census The Town Clerk conducts the annual census of Northfield’s households and publishes the results in a printed residents’ list (commonly known as the "Street List"). The publication contains an alphabetical-numerical list of all residents seventeen and older. The Town Clerk also prepares a non-public list of persons age three and older for the Pioneer Regional School District. 1. Nomination & Petition Papers The first step to running for office or placing a question on the ballot is to gather the required number of signatures of registered voters on petition papers. (A person may not have to complete nomination papers if he/she is nominated through the Town Caucus Process.  Please see the Town Clerk for specific details.)  The number of signatures depends on the office or the type of question. The Town Clerk supplies the petition papers. Candidates or question proponents must gather the required number of signatures on the petition papers supplied by the Town Clerk. ## Annual Town Election

The Annual Town Election is the first Monday in March. All precincts vote at the Ruth B. Smith Auditorium, at Town Hall, 6 Prospect Street.  The last day to register to vote for the Annual Town Election is ten days prior to the election.

Nomination papers must be taken out to run for an elected position in Orange. Only registered voters in Orange can take out papers and run for an elected office. Nomination papers will be available in the Town Clerk's Office in December. 2025 Annual Town Election – 
Key Dates & Details
Election Day: Tuesday, May 20, 2025

  * Moderator – 1 seat, 3-year term

### OPEN MEETING LAW UPDATES                 On March 28, 2025, Governor Healey signed into law a supplemental budget bill which, among other things, extends the temporary provisions pertaining to the Open Meeting Law to June 30, 2027. Specifically, this further extension allows public bodies to continue holding meetings remotely without a quorum of the public body physically present at a meeting location, and to provide "adequate, alternative" access to remote meetings. The language does not make any substantive changes to the Open Meeting Law other than extending the expiration date of the temporary provisions regarding remote meetings from March 31, 2025 to June 30, 2027.                                                                                                                                       

  1. Remote Meeting Law Extension June 30, 2027

The Oak Bluffs Town Clerk’s office provides many services to our community. We work cooperatively with other town departments as well as the State of Massachusetts. Since 1880, we have been the keepers of official records and documents - town meeting records, vital records, Zoning and Town Bylaws, and Town Reports. Our office tracks elected and appointed members of various positions and committees.

## Responsibilities

We are responsible for all facets of every town, state and federal election. All public meetings are posted through this office and are found in the entryway of our Town Hall. This office creates an annual town census, maintains voter lists and provides proof of residency for the Steamship Authority. We welcome any questions you may have about the Town of Oak Bluffs.

## Services

Contact the Town Clerk’s Office regarding:

  * Absentee Ballets and Voter Registration for all Elections and Referenda
  * Auctioneer Permits
  * Bills of Sale for Martha’s Vineyard Camp Meeting Association - $10 first page, $2 thereafter
  * Business Certificates - $40 for 4 years (Doing Business As…)
  * Census
  * Certified Copies of Birth, Marriage and Death Certificates (Vital Records)- $10
  * Dog Licenses - $10 or $6 for spayed or neutered. Late fee starts March 1st (add $10)
  * Intention of Marriage/ Marriage License Application Process - $25
  * Junk License
  * Proof of Residency (for Steamship Authority)
  * Raffle and Bazaar Permits
  * Zoning and General By-Laws

### OPEN MEETING LAW UPDATES                 On March 28, 2025, Governor Healey signed into law a supplemental budget bill which, among other things, extends the temporary provisions pertaining to the Open Meeting Law to June 30, 2027. Specifically, this further extension allows public bodies to continue holding meetings remotely without a quorum of the public body physically present at a meeting location, and to provide "adequate, alternative" access to remote meetings. The language does not make any substantive changes to the Open Meeting Law other than extending the expiration date of the temporary provisions regarding remote meetings from March 31, 2025 to June 30, 2027.                                                                                                                                       

  1. Remote Meeting Law Extension June 30, 2027

The Oak Bluffs Town Clerk’s office provides many services to our community. We work cooperatively with other town departments as well as the State of Massachusetts. Since 1880, we have been the keepers of official records and documents - town meeting records, vital records, Zoning and Town Bylaws, and Town Reports. Our office tracks elected and appointed members of various positions and committees.

## Responsibilities

We are responsible for all facets of every town, state and federal election. All public meetings are posted through this office and are found in the entryway of our Town Hall. This office creates an annual town census, maintains voter lists and provides proof of residency for the Steamship Authority. We welcome any questions you may have about the Town of Oak Bluffs.

## Services

Contact the Town Clerk’s Office regarding:

  * Absentee Ballets and Voter Registration for all Elections and Referenda
  * Auctioneer Permits
  * Bills of Sale for Martha’s Vineyard Camp Meeting Association - $10 first page, $2 thereafter
  * Business Certificates - $40 for 4 years (Doing Business As…)
  * Census
  * Certified Copies of Birth, Marriage and Death Certificates (Vital Records)- $10
  * Dog Licenses - $10 or $6 for spayed or neutered. Late fee starts March 1st (add $10)
  * Intention of Marriage/ Marriage License Application Process - $25
  * Junk License
  * Proof of Residency (for Steamship Authority)
  * Raffle and Bazaar Permits
  * Zoning and General By-Laws

# Town Clerk

The Town Clerk's responsibilities include overseeing elections, registering voters, recording official actions of Town Meeting, conducting the annual census, and preserving official town documents. In addition, the Clerk records births, marriages and deaths, administers the oath of office to town officials, issues licenses, posts meetings of governmental bodies, provides access to public records and provides local officials with information regarding the Open Meeting Law and Conflict of Interest Law.

The mission of this office is to serve as a resource to residents with respect to all matters within the Town Clerk's jurisdiction in a timely and courteous manner.

## Welcome to Pelham, Mass

Image

Pelham is a small, pleasant town perched on the ridge that divides the Connecticut River's Pioneer Valley from Quabbin Reservoir and central Massachusetts. The eastern one-third of the town is state owned land, part of the Reservoir watershed. Almost one-third of Pelham's original land area is now part of the Quabbin Reservoir, which was constructed in the 1930's. Daniel Shays Highway, now part of Route 202, was built as part of the reservoir project.

About 1280 people now live in Pelham. The Pelham School System is the Town's largest employer. Most employed persons work out of town at businesses, nearby colleges and the University of Massachusetts. Pelham is home to many retired people who enjoy the environment and cultural opportunities of the region.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Town Clerk

The Town Clerk has many functions which are regulated by Massachusetts General Laws and Town By-laws.

The Town Clerk is the keeper of town records and responsible for maintaining records including but not limited to all town actions, vital records, voter records, licenses, permits, appointments and oaths to name a few.

The Town Clerk is the chief election official for the town responsible for the conduct of local, state and federal elections; administration of voter registration and local census.

Justice of the Peace services are offered during Town Clerk Office Hours.

Records Access Officers (RAO) have been assigned to coordinate and respond to requests for Public Records.

Town Clerk does not collect property tax or excise tax – those taxes go through the Tax Collector’s office.

Records Access Officers

(July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025)

  On November 5, 2024, 1170 ballots were cast.  There was a total of 519 ballots cast by mail and

Phillipston was fortunate to put 4 new residents on the election staff, and their help is 
appreciated.  The tallies were counted by midnight, and reports were finished by 1:00am.  Harris 
and Waltz received 438 votes and Trump and Vance received 697 here in Phillipston.  Donald 
Trump won the election for president for the country.
