# Town Clerk

The Office of the Town Clerk is the doorway to local government.

The Town Clerk is responsible for preparing and conducting all elections, including providing nomination papers, campaign finance forms, voter registration, absentee ballots, and tallying the votes. After the election, the Clerk administers the oath of office to each elected and appointed official.

During the Annual and Special Town Meetings, the Town Clerk records and certifies the minutes of the meetings. All by-law changes must be submitted to the Attorney General for approval before they become law.

Other responsibilities of the Town Clerk include compiling the Annual Street List, issuing dog licenses, birth, marriage and death certificates, business certificates, and keeping records for the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, and the Conservation Commission.

The Town Clerk's position is multi-faceted, and perhaps the most important aspect is its unwritten role in public relations and customer service. In fact, when people have any questions about the Town, they often call the Town House to ask the Clerk. You can also take a look on this site at the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) page, and find some answers.

## Online Services

The Town Clerk offers online services for ordering Birth, Death, and Marriage Certificates, as well as the processing of dog licenses if a current rabies certificate is on file.

For online services for the Town Clerk, visit the UNIPAY Website.

Secretary of State, Elections Division 6 Town Hall Drive Princeton, MA 01541 978-464-2103 (phone) TOWN OF PRINCETON 978-464-2106 (fax) townclerk@town.princeton.ma.us MASSACHUSETTS Office of the Town Clerk NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUDIT (ELECTION RESULTS – PRECINCT 1) Section 109A of Chapter 54 of the General Laws requires random post-election audits to be conducted after presidential elections. Under this law, 3 per cent of all precincts in Massachusetts must be hand-counted. The selection is done by random, publicly verifiable, non-computerized drawing supervised by the Secretary within 48 hours of the close of polls. The law provides for a hand-count of only certain specified races, where more than one candidate is printed on the ballot, and a statewide ballot question, which is also randomly selected. On Thursday, November 7, 2024, Precinct 1 of the Town of Princeton, was one of 3 per cent of all precincts in Massachusetts selected for the post-election audit of results for the November 5, 2024 State Election. Pursuant to Section 109A of General Laws Chapter 54, G.L. c. 54 § 109A(d)(1) and 950 CMR § 46.01(1), the audit will be conducted on: Monday, November 11, 2024 at 9:00AM Location: Town Hall Annex, located at 4 Town Hall Drive, Princeton, MA 01541. The administration of the audit is conducted by the Registrars of Voters. The Board of Registrars can designate the local election official to perform the audit. If the clerk is designated to perform the audit, the registrars do not need to be present. Members of the public who wish to attend this audit are asked to contact townclerk@town.princeton.ma.us. Respectfully, Alissa K. Horsung Alissa K. Horsung, Princeton Town Clerk, Local Election Official and Registrar of Voters cc. The Clerk performs key statutory duties under Massachusetts General Laws (MGL) and provides essential services to residents, businesses, and visitors. ### The Town Clerk Serves You As: Chief Election Official – MGL Ch. 41 § 1; Ch. 54; Ch. 51  Oversees all aspects of National, State, and Local elections. Recording Officer – MGL Ch. 41 § 15  Records and certifies all official actions of the Town. Registrar of Vital Statistics – MGL Ch. 46; Ch. 41 § 19  Registers all vital events occurring within the community and those occurring elsewhere to local residents. Records and preserves original birth, marriage, and death records. The Town of Provincetown is providing voters with important information regarding In-Person Early Voting, ballot drop-off locations, and Election Day parking for the November 3, 2026 Election. ... #### 2026 State Primary Election - Official Results # Town Clerk ## About the Town Clerk’s Office The Town Clerk’s Office serves as the primary hub for the Town’s official records, licensing, and elections. The Clerk performs key statutory duties under Massachusetts General Laws (MGL) and provides essential services to residents, businesses, and visitors. ### The Town Clerk Serves You As: Chief Election Official – MGL Ch. 41 § 1; Ch. 54; Ch. 51  Oversees all aspects of National, State, and Local elections. Directs the preparation of ballots, polling places, voting equipment, and voter lists; certifies nomination papers and initiative petitions. Recording Officer – MGL Ch. 41 § 15  Records and certifies all official actions of the Town. Registrar of Vital Statistics – MGL Ch. 46; Ch. 41 § 19  Registers all vital events occurring within the community and those occurring elsewhere to local residents. Records and preserves original birth, marriage, and death records. Public Records Officer – MGL Ch. 66; Ch. 4 § 7(26)  Administers the oath of office to all elected and appointed members of local committees and boards. * Town Archives Cemetery Services * Cemetery Lot Sales Other Services * Notary Services Guidelines ### Contact Us 1. #### Elizabeth Paine Town Clerk Email Elizabeth Paine (epaine@provincetown-ma.gov) More Information 2. #### Ana Ruiz Assistant Town Clerk Email Ana Ruiz (aruiz@provincetown-ma.gov) 3. #### Town Clerk Physical Address 260 Commercial Street Provincetown, MA 02657 Phone: (508) 487-7013 Fax: (508) 487-9560 Office Hours Monday through Thursday 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Friday 8:00 am to 12 noon ### News 1. #### Early Voting Hours, Ballot Drop-Off Locations & Important Information for November 3, 2026 Election The Town of Provincetown is providing voters with important information regarding In-Person Early Voting, ballot drop-off locations, and Election Day parking for the November 3, 2026 Election. Town Hall 41 S Main Street Randolph MA 02368 # Clerk / Registrar ## Campaign Finance Deadlines * Wednesday, January 20, 2027, until 5pm, Year End Reports are due The office of the Town Clerk and Registrar strives to be a vital part of local government. We are committed to serving as the link between residents, businesses, local governing bodies, and agencies of government at all levels; maintaining and preserving public records, and acting in the best interest of the community by providing innovative, efficient, quality customer service. We are committed to upholding the integrity of the Town's democratic process. # Town Clerk

## Overview

Register to Vote, check/update voter information

Vote by Mail

Town Census Instructions

2026 Census Form

2026 Dog Licensing Worksheet

## Description

Often considered the doorway to local government, the Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for residents and visitors alike. The Town Clerk is the chief election official, recording official, registrar of vital records, public records official, and licensing officer. The Town Clerk oversees the polling places and the conduct of all elections and election-related activity, and records all actions of Town Meeting. The Clerk's Office maintains the municipal code, the official Town bulletin board, oaths of office, appointments and resignations of all Town Officials. The Clerk's Office issues state licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, business licenses and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, raffle/bazaar permits and certified requests for public documents. This office responds to inquiries from the public as well as from other departments, boards and committees.

## Mission

It is the mission of this office to be a reliable provider of information and quality services to the community and its residents, and to work cooperatively and in concert with all departments, boards and committees while complying with state and local statutes.

# Town Clerk

## Services

  * Annual Town Census
  * Commissioners to Qualify
  * Licensing of Dogs can be done in person, by mail or online. Register online starting April 1st of each year. View the printable application.
  * Limited Notary Services (PDF)
  * Recording and issuance of Vital Records (births, marriages, and deaths)
  * Town Meeting and Election Records
  * Historic District filings

# Key Dates

### 2026 Elections / Town Meetings

  * March 3, 2026 Special State Primary
  * March 31, 2026 Special State Election
  * April 11, 2026 Annual Town Meeting
  * May 19, 2026 Local Election
  * September 1, 2026 State Primary
  * September 14, 2026 Fall Town Meeting

### *Town Election and Town Meeting dates are subject to change per issuance of the Warrant

### Register to Vote

Registration forms can be found in the back door vestibule of Town Hall, sent by mail-in, done through the Registry of Motor Vehicles, or online at the Secretary of the Commonwealth website.

### Voting on Election Day

Voting on Election Day takes place at the following locations:

  * Precinct 1: Town Hall Annex, 26 Broadway
  * Precinct 2: St. Mary's Episcopal Church, 24 Broadway
  * Precinct 3: Rockport Community House, 58 Broadway
  * Election Day Voting Hours: 7 am to 8 pm

### FAQs

How do I obtain a certified birth, marriage or death certificate?
    

To obtain a Certified Copy of a Birth, Marriage or Death Certificate:

Fill out the Vital Records Request Form 

Mail it with a self-addressed, stamped envelope and $10.00 for the first and $5.00 for each additional certified copy to:

Town Clerks Office

P.O. Box 429

Rockport MA 01966

Be sure to include the name and date of event for the record being requested.

If you need any other information, please call the Town Clerk’s office at 978-546-6894.

How do I register to vote?
    

On the Secretary of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts website.

In person at the Town Clerks office.

At the Registry of Motor Vehicles and other State registration points.

How do I obtain a marriage license?
    

A couple wishing to be married in Massachusetts may file intentions in any City or Town Hall in Massachusetts.

To apply for a marriage license:

  1. Both parties must complete the Marriage Intention forms together and in-person at Town Hall.
  2. Provide a valid form of identification.
  3. There is a mandatory 72 hour waiting period before they can be picked up.
  4. Intentions are valid for 60 days.
  5. The fee in Rockport is $30.00.

Please call the office with any questions 978-546-6894.

The Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing accurate election information and ensuring every eligible voter has the opportunity to participate in Rochester's local government.

Voters elect Town officials and vote on any ballot questions appearing on the ballot.

Town Meeting Quorum

A minimum number of registered voters must be present before Town Meeting may conduct business.





Meeting  | Quorum
--- | ---
Annual Town Meeting  | 75 voters
Special Town Meeting ($25,000+ appropriations or zoning)  | 50 voters
Special Town Meeting (under $25,000)  | 15 voters

If a quorum is not reached, the Moderator may recess or adjourn the meeting in accordance with Town bylaws.

How Town Meeting Works

Every registered Rochester voter has the right to speak and vote at Town Meeting. Business is conducted according to the Town's bylaws and parliamentary procedure. Most articles require a majority vote, while certain matters, such as zoning amendments, require a two-thirds vote.

Non-residents may address Town Meeting only with the permission of the voters.

Get Involved

Residents are encouraged to:

  * Review the Town Meeting Warrant before the meeting.
  * Read Finance Committee recommendations.
  * Attend informational sessions when available.
  * Register to vote before the deadline.
  * Participate respectfully in debate and voting.

Election & Town Meeting Resources

# Town Clerk & Elections

***The Town Clerk's office is having difficulty with the new phone system. Please refrain from calling and email: Records@rutlandma.gov

Image: IMG_8641

The Rutland Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing efficient service, to all residents and non-residents alike, competently and courteously, while keeping the integrity of the Office.

The Town Clerk is the chief election official, recording official, registrar of vital records (births, deaths, and marriages), and public records official.

The Town Clerk's office issues state licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, business certificates (DBA's) and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, raffles/bazaar permits, and requests for public documents. Beginning January 2012 the Town Clerk's office will no longer issue fishing and hunting licenses.

The Town Clerk is responsible for all elections and voter registrations, as well as overseeing the polling place and the conduct of all elections. The office records all actions and certifies all official actions of the Town, including town meeting legislation and appropriations. The Town Clerk's Office administers the oaths of office and maintains appointments and resignations of all Town Officials.

# Town Clerk & Elections

***The Town Clerk's office is having difficulty with the new phone system. Please refrain from calling and email: Records@rutlandma.gov

Image: IMG_8641

The Rutland Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing efficient service, to all residents and non-residents alike, competently and courteously, while keeping the integrity of the Office.

The Town Clerk is the chief election official, recording official, registrar of vital records (births, deaths, and marriages), and public records official.

The Town Clerk's office issues state licenses and permits, including marriage licenses, business certificates (DBA's) and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, raffles/bazaar permits, and requests for public documents. Beginning January 2012 the Town Clerk's office will no longer issue fishing and hunting licenses.

The Town Clerk is responsible for all elections and voter registrations, as well as overseeing the polling place and the conduct of all elections. The office records all actions and certifies all official actions of the Town, including town meeting legislation and appropriations. The Town Clerk's Office administers the oaths of office and maintains appointments and resignations of all Town Officials.

# Town Clerk

## Mission Statement

Working with the Board of Registrars, the Town Clerk ensures that all elections are held in accordance with federal and state laws. The Town Clerk maintains vital records, issues certificates and licenses, and conducts the Town census. The Parking Clerk receives payment for parking fines and resolves complaints. The Town Clerk provides the following services:

  * Register voters, conduct elections
  * Issue licenses and permits, such as marriage licenses, birth and death certificates, and dog licenses
  * Conduct census
  * Issue reports

Town Clerk 
The Town Clerk’s Office acts as Sandisfield’s central point for official records and municipal 
administration. We issue birth, death, and marriage certificates, business (DBA) certificates, 
and dog licenses. In addition, the office manages essential town government functions, 
including conducting the annual town census, overseeing all municipal, state, and federal 
elections, and supporting Town Meetings. 
Beyond vital records and elections, the Clerk’s Office maintains Town Meeting warrants and 
the minutes of boards and committees, ensuring these records remain accessible to the 
public. The Town Clerk also serves as the Town’s liaison to the Attorney General’s Office for 
all zoning and bylaw submissions and approvals.

# Official 2026 Annual Town Meeting and Town Election Results Posted

Town Manager Posted on May 12, 2026

Official results for the May 4, 2026 Annual Town Meeting and the May 7, 2026 Annual Town Election are now available on the Town of Sandwich website: 

  * May 4, 2026 Annual Town Meeting Results
  * May 7 Annual Town Election Results

The Town of Sandwich extends its sincere thanks to all residents who participated in the 2026 Annual Town Meeting and Annual Town Election. These important civic events reflect the community’s continued commitment to thoughtful discussion and active participation in local government. The Town also extends its appreciation to the many individuals whose hard work made these events possible, including Town staff and volunteers. 

## Annual Town Meeting- May 4, 2026 

Town Meeting brought 553 Sandwich votes together to consider a wide range of issues impacting the community, including the Fiscal Year 2027 operating budget, capital improvements, infrastructure investments, community preservation projects, and other important initiatives that will help shape Sandwich’s future. Town leadership appreciates the residents' support on all of the financial articles. 

Official results and minutes from the 2026 Annual Town Meeting can be found here.

Highlights: 

  * Article 2 - FY 2027 Budget was passed
  * Article 18- Citizens' Petition- Allow Carry of Firearms in Town Buildings was postponed indefinitely 

## Annual Town Election- May 7, 2026

Town leadership would like to thank all of the candidates who stepped forward to serve the community and all of the residents who took the time to stay informed and engaged throughout the process. The official results of the 2026 Annual Town Election can be found here.

Highlights: 

  * Residents elected David D. Sullivan as the newest member of the Select Board, replacing Robert J. George, who retired from the Board.  Sullivan will serve a three-year term from 2026-2029. 
  * Residents reelected David Sampson to the Select Board.  He will serve a three-year term from 2026-2029. 
  * For the two contested races on the ballot:
    * Residents elected Tobin Craig Wirt as Constable
    * Residents elected Jonathan David Finn as Trustee of the Weston Memorial Fund 

## 2025 Annual Town Report 

In addition, the Town of Sandwich 2025 Annual Town Report is now available online. The report provides residents with a comprehensive overview of Town operations, accomplishments, finances, and department updates from the past year.

Residents are encouraged to visit the Town website to review these materials and stay connected with ongoing Town news and initiatives.

# Elections & Voting

## Elections and Voter Registration

The Town Clerk is authorized by state law to administer elections and elections-related processes and functions. There also are three Registrars of Voters who are appointed by the Board of Selectmen, each serving a three- year term.

The Town Clerk administers the day-to-day process for elections.

### Election Documents and Results

### Precinct List

### Vote by Mail Application 

### State Election Information & In-person Early Voting Schedule

General Duties

The Scituate Town Clerk administers nomination and election processes, registers voters, conducts the annual municipal census and certifies applications and documents for veterans' bonuses. The Town Clerk also verifies residences for state colleges and universities, travel certificates and social security administration. The Town Clerk prepares and provides all statistics on elections and census, and general assistance for citizens, political parties and members of the press.

Elections Administration

The Scituate Town Clerk conducts all presidential primaries, state primaries, and state and presidential elections. The Town Clerk also conducts the Annual Town Election. The responsibilities of the Town Clerk include: voter registration; supplying nomination papers for candidates, initiatives and referenda; certification of signatures on all nomination papers and petitions; printing ballots for Town elections; maintenance of elections equipment; supervision of poll workers; tallying elections results; and maintaining and preserving the records of the election.

List of Voters

The Town Clerk maintains the voters roll for Scituate. The Town Clerk endeavors to maintain as accurate a list as possible for use at the polls on election day. Voters are removed from the voters list because of death or a move outside of the Town and voters are added to the list as they register. In addition, all voters who change party affiliation are processed.

# Elections & Voting

## Elections and Voter Registration

The Town Clerk is authorized by state law to administer elections and elections-related processes and functions. There also are three Registrars of Voters who are appointed by the Board of Selectmen, each serving a three- year term.

The Town Clerk administers the day-to-day process for elections.

### Election Documents and Results

### Precinct List

### Vote by Mail Application 

### State Election Information & In-person Early Voting Schedule

General Duties

The Scituate Town Clerk administers nomination and election processes, registers voters, conducts the annual municipal census and certifies applications and documents for veterans' bonuses. The Town Clerk also verifies residences for state colleges and universities, travel certificates and social security administration. The Town Clerk prepares and provides all statistics on elections and census, and general assistance for citizens, political parties and members of the press.

Elections Administration

The Scituate Town Clerk conducts all presidential primaries, state primaries, and state and presidential elections. The Town Clerk also conducts the Annual Town Election. The responsibilities of the Town Clerk include: voter registration; supplying nomination papers for candidates, initiatives and referenda; certification of signatures on all nomination papers and petitions; printing ballots for Town elections; maintenance of elections equipment; supervision of poll workers; tallying elections results; and maintaining and preserving the records of the election.

List of Voters

The Town Clerk maintains the voters roll for Scituate. The Town Clerk endeavors to maintain as accurate a list as possible for use at the polls on election day. Voters are removed from the voters list because of death or a move outside of the Town and voters are added to the list as they register. In addition, all voters who change party affiliation are processed.

## Duties and Responsibilities

### Census

  * Conducts the annual town census.
  * Prepares the street list of residents and the school list.
  * Furnishes the jury list to the Office of the Jury Commissioner.

### Elections

  * Oversees polling places, election officers, and the general conduct of all elections.
  * Directs preparation of ballots, polling places, voting equipment and voting lists.
  * Administers campaign finance laws.
  * Certifies nomination papers and initiative petitions.
  * Serves on the local Board of Registrars.
  * Supervises voter registration and absentee ballots.
  * Prepares, records and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth.

### Licenses
  * Certifies copies of all town records.
  * Records and preserves original birth, marriage, and death records, providing the basis for the Commonwealth's central vital registration system.
  * Provides certified copies of vital records and conducts or assists with genealogical research for members of the public.
  * Is responsible for maintenance, disposition, and preservation of municipal archival records and materials.
  * Maintains records of adopted municipal codes, general bylaws and zoning bylaws, resignations, appointments, petitions, publications, budgets, election results and town meeting minutes and financial statements.
  * Submits general bylaws and zoning bylaws to Attorney General for approval.
  * Maintains the Annual List of Residents.

# Elections & Voting

VOTER REGISTRATION & STATUS UPDATES

To check your voter registration status, update address and/or party, update name or register / Pre-register to vote, please use the link below to the Secretary of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts website: https://www.sec.state.ma.us/ovr/

Absentee Ballot applications are available in our office or on the Town Clerk page. If you want to be put on the permanent absentee ballot mailing list please fill out the form and check off "For all elections". If you know you will be out of Town for a certain election you can request an absentee ballot several weeks before an election. Remember If you are voting in a Primary and are Unenrolled (Independent) you must write down what party ballot you want.

# Town Clerk

WELCOME to the Town Clerk’s Office web site. We hope you find the following information helpful and informative concerning the services we provide to the residents of Sheffield.

The Town Clerk is the official record keeper for the Town of Sheffield. The Town Clerk’s Office also handles town census, voter registration, elections and issues a number of licenses and certificates described below.

### Services offered by the Town Clerk’s Office include the following:

  * Vital statistics – birth certificates, marriage certificates and death certificates
  * Posting of all meetings for all municipal boards and committees
  * Voter Registration
  * Town Political Calendar
  * Census Forms
  * Residency Certification
  * Town Meeting Warrants and Minutes
  * Business Certificates (d/b/a)
  * Notarization of documents
  * Payment of non-criminal complaint violations

### The following licenses can be obtained at the Town Clerk’s Office:

  * Marriage License
  * Dog Licenses

### The following documents may be obtained from the Town Clerk’s Office:

  * Special Permit Application Forms
  * Zoning By-Laws
  * Zoning Maps
  * General By-Laws
  * Sub-division Control Booklets
  * Board of Appeals Filing Packets
  * Historic District Filing Form

# Town Clerk

WELCOME to the Town Clerk’s Office web site. We hope you find the following information helpful and informative concerning the services we provide to the residents of Sheffield.

The Town Clerk is the official record keeper for the Town of Sheffield. The Town Clerk’s Office also handles town census, voter registration, elections and issues a number of licenses and certificates described below.

### Services offered by the Town Clerk’s Office include the following:

  * Vital statistics – birth certificates, marriage certificates and death certificates
  * Posting of all meetings for all municipal boards and committees
  * Voter Registration
  * Town Political Calendar
  * Census Forms
  * Residency Certification
  * Town Meeting Warrants and Minutes
  * Business Certificates (d/b/a)
  * Notarization of documents
  * Payment of non-criminal complaint violations

### The following licenses can be obtained at the Town Clerk’s Office:

  * Marriage License
  * Dog Licenses

### The following documents may be obtained from the Town Clerk’s Office:

  * Special Permit Application Forms
  * Zoning By-Laws
  * Zoning Maps
  * General By-Laws
  * Sub-division Control Booklets
  * Board of Appeals Filing Packets
  * Historic District Filing Form

# Annual Town Election May 5, 2026

# Tuesday, MAY 5, 2026 - POLLS ARE OPEN 7:00 AM TO 8:00 PM

# Annual Town Election May 5, 2026 Official Results

# Sample Ballot

Vote By Mail Application

Click HERE for polling locations and election and voter information

The state legislature passed the Votes Act of 2022 allowing "no-excuse" vote by mail. A Vote by Mail Application must be filed with the Town Clerk's office in order to receive a ballot by mail.  The deadline to apply is 5 PM on Tuesday, April 28.   Absentee ballots application by mail must be received by 5 PM on Tuesday, April 28.  The deadline for absentee voting at the counter is Noon on Monday, May 4.  You can find more information on who qualifies for an absentee ballot HERE. All completed ballots must be received by the close of polls on Tuesday, May 5 at the Town Clerk's Office.

Voter registration deadline for the May 5, 2026 Town Election is 5:00 PM on Friday, April 24, 2026.

# Running for Election to Town Meeting:

Town Meeting serves as the Town's legislative body under the provisions of Chapter 553 of the Acts of 1953, known as the Representative Town Meeting Act. Town Meeting is responsible for taking all action normally associated with that of a legislative body in the American system of democracy including decisions about the Town's budgets, local bylaws and other matters. The legislative body of Shrewsbury is composed of 240 Town Meeting Members representing ten (10) precincts for staggered three (3) year terms. 

Qualified candidates (registered voter in Shrewsbury) had their name placed on the ballot by filing nomination papers with the Town Clerk by 5:00 PM on March 17, 2026 and receiving the minimum of ten (10) signatures of registered voters in their precinct. 
If you have taken out nomination papers and the signatures have been certified, you are able to withdraw your name from the ballot if you change your mind. The last day to withdraw your name is 5:00 PM on April 2, 2026. 

# Campaign Finance & Filing Requirements:

 (Town Meeting Members are exempt from campaign finance)

# Running for Election to Town Meeting:

Town Meeting serves as the Town's legislative body under the provisions of Chapter 553 of the Acts of 1953, known as the Representative Town Meeting Act. Town Meeting is responsible for taking all action normally associated with that of a legislative body in the American system of democracy including decisions about the Town's budgets, local bylaws and other matters. The legislative body of Shrewsbury is composed of 240 Town Meeting Members representing ten (10) precincts for staggered three (3) year terms. 

Qualified candidates (registered voter in Shrewsbury) had their name placed on the ballot by filing nomination papers with the Town Clerk by 5:00 PM on March 17, 2026 and receiving the minimum of ten (10) signatures of registered voters in their precinct. 
If you have taken out nomination papers and the signatures have been certified, you are able to withdraw your name from the ballot if you change your mind. The last day to withdraw your name is 5:00 PM on April 2, 2026. 

# Campaign Finance & Filing Requirements:

 (Town Meeting Members are exempt from campaign finance)

All currently serving Elected Officials should have filed their year-end Campaign Finance Reports by January 21, 2025.

All candidates for Town-wide elected office must file finance forms with the Town Clerk if they have a campaign committee and are raising funds: 

April 27, 2026 - Eight (8) days before the local election - Pre-election report

June 4, 2026 - Thirty (30) days after local election - Post election report

If no money is raised, a candidate may fill out a CPF M109 which covers the requirements for pre and post election, however a year end report must still be filed. More information on Campaign Finance can be found at the Office of Campaign and Political Finance website at https://www.ocpf.us/

The Annual Town Meeting will be held on Monday, May 18, 2026 at 7:00pm in the Oak Middle School Auditorium, 45 Oak Street, Shrewsbury.  Please be advised that if Town Meeting does not conclude on Monday, May 18, 2026, it will continue to Tuesday, May 19, 2026 at 7:00pm.

## About Elections

The Somerville Elections Department oversees all local, state, and federal elections, registers voters, and keeps election-related public records, including campaign finance reports. The Department also conducts the Annual City Census. On this page, you can find information on registering to vote, find your polling place, learn how to run for office in Somerville, and more.

The Town Clerk is the communication spokesperson to and for the local citizenry. ## Online Voter Registration Now Available

Secretary of the Commonwealth William Francis Galvin has announced that online vottHer registration is now available in the Commonwealth through the portal launched by his office. This important advancement will make registration easier and more convenient as well as cut costs relating to the printing of voter registration forms.

Massachusetts citizens can apply online by visiting Secretary Galvin’s website and clicking the “Massachusetts Register to Vote Online” button to access the online application system. Any Massachusetts citizen who has a valid identification card issued by the Registry of Motor Vehicles will be able to use the online system to apply to register to vote, update their address or change their party enrollment.

Massachusetts citizens who do not have identification issued by the Registry of Motor Vehicles can still complete an application online which they can print, sign and mail or hand-deliver to their local election official.

 

* * *

## Elections and Voter Registration Information:

### To register to vote, you must:

  * Be a U.S. Citizen
  * Be a Massachusetts resident
  * Be at least 18 years old on or before the next election

### Go to the Secretary of the Commonwealth to:

  * Learn how to Register to Vote
  * Obtain a Voter Registration Form
  * Apply for an Absentee Ballot
  * Check the Status of your Mail in Ballot during elections

### Absentee Ballot Application/Mail In Voter Application

If you are not able to vote on Election Day, you may apply for an absentee ballot. This should be done no later than 2 weeks before any given election. You may also vote absentee at the Clerk’s Office in person; however, this must be done no later than 12 noon on the day preceding the election. For more information, you may visit the Secretary of State’s website for info, or call the Clerk’s Office at (413) 527-8392.

### Polling Location

We are now a two precinct town. Both precincts are located in the Town Hall (Senior Center), 210 College Highway. The Annual Town Election is held on the third Tuesday of May and the Annual Town meeting is held on the first Tuesday of May (unless it is changed or postponed) 

### Town Meeting Results

The Town of Southampton has an open Town Meeting form of government. Every registered voter is eligible to participate in the meeting as a voting member. Town Meeting is held annually on the first Tuesday in May at the William Norris Elementary School Gymnasium (Town Meeting Calendar).--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Town Clerk also serves as the Chief Election Official and is directly responsible to the 
Voters of the Town.  The Town Clerk oversees the eight polling locations and the conduct of all 
elections and election related activity such as early voting in person and by mail.  The Clerk 
works with the Board of Registrars to promote and maintain voter registration and voter records.  
We prepare, record and report official election results to the Secretary of the Commonwealth.  
Our office prepares ballots, voting equipment, voting lists and certifies nomination papers as 
well as initiative petitions.  Our office records and certifies all official actions of Town, 
including Town Meeting legislation and appropriations, Planning and Zoning Board of Appeals 
Decisions, signs all notes for borrowing and is the keeper of the Town Seal. 
 
The Town Clerk can provide certified copies of all vital records we have on file as well as 
preserves original birth, marriage and death records.  Our office provides Justice of the Peace, 
Notary and Commissioner to Qualify services.  The office conducts the annual Town census and 
provides access to public records in compliance with the State Public Records Law and 
corresponding regulations.

## Overview

Often considered the core of local government, the Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for local residents and citizens at large. The Town Clerk is the keeper of town records, the chief election official, a member of the Board of Registrars, official keeper of the Town Seal, registers all vital events occurring within the community and those events occurring elsewhere to local residents. The Town Clerk records and preserves birth, marriage and death records and provides certified copies of these records upon request.

The Town Clerk also serves as the Chief Election Official and is directly responsible to the 
Voters of the Town.  The Town Clerk oversees the eight polling locations and the conduct of all 
elections and election related activity such as early voting in person and by mail.  The Clerk 
works with the Board of Registrars to promote and maintain voter registration and voter records.  
We prepare, record and report official election results to the Secretary of the Commonwealth.  
Our office prepares ballots, voting equipment, voting lists and certifies nomination papers as 
well as initiative petitions.  Our office records and certifies all official actions of Town, 
including Town Meeting legislation and appropriations, Planning and Zoning Board of Appeals 
Decisions, signs all notes for borrowing and is the keeper of the Town Seal. 
 
The Town Clerk can provide certified copies of all vital records we have on file as well as 
preserves original birth, marriage and death records.  Our office provides Justice of the Peace, 
Notary and Commissioner to Qualify services.  The office conducts the annual Town census and 
provides access to public records in compliance with the State Public Records Law and 
corresponding regulations.

## Overview

Often considered the core of local government, the Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for local residents and citizens at large. The Town Clerk is the keeper of town records, the chief election official, a member of the Board of Registrars, official keeper of the Town Seal, registers all vital events occurring within the community and those events occurring elsewhere to local residents. The Town Clerk records and preserves birth, marriage and death records and provides certified copies of these records upon request.

Welcome to Massachusetts!

| Town Clerk | Updated

When are elections held?

Presidential primaries are held once every four years in March.

State elections occur every other year in even numbered years. The State Primary is held in September and the State Election in November.

Town elections The Annual Town Election in Sudbury is on the last Monday in March. Special Elections may be called by the Select Board.

The Annual Town Meeting in Sudbury is held on the first Monday in May. Special Town Meetings may also be called during the year.

# Town Meeting & Election

The Town of Sutton is governed by General Bylaws, Home Rule Charter, Massachusetts General Law, and other relevant statutes. The Town's form of government, an elected, five-member Select Board appoints a Town Manager to administer the daily operation of the Town. The Town's legislative body is Open Town Meeting. According to the General Bylaws, the Town Manager must submit a balanced budget annually to the Select Board and Finance and Warrant Advisory Committee. The budget is reviewed by the Select Board before being moved to the Finance and Warrant Advisory Committee. The Finance and Warrant Advisory Committee reviews the annual operating budget and other warrant articles and submits their recommendations to Town Meeting. Town Meeting then votes to adopt the annual operating budget and other warrant articles at the Annual Town Meeting. Information related to the budget process, town meeting and the town election can be found below.

# Election

The 2026 election season includes two important statewide elections: the State Primary Election on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, and the State General Election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. These elections determine who will represent Massachusetts at the federal, state, county, and local levels.

### State General Election – November 3, 2026

The General Election is when all registered voters cast their ballots to elect public officials. The ballot will include candidates for offices such as Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Treasurer, Auditor, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, State Senator, State Representative, and other offices that may vary by community.

### Important Election Dates

  * State General Election: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
  * General Election Voter Registration Deadline: October 24, 2026
  * General Election Early Voting: October 17–30, 2026
  * General Election Vote-by-Mail Application Deadline: October 27, 2026

# Town Meeting

The Town of Sutton follows a traditional open town meeting process, which provides an important platform for residents to engage in local governance. Town meetings are typically held twice a year, in the spring (the 2nd Monday of May) and in the fall (the 3rd Monday of October). Voters gather to discuss and decide on key community issues, including budgets, zoning laws, and other local policies. In this forum, residents can propose, debate, and vote on a range of topics, ensuring that decisions reflect the collective voice of the town. The meeting is designed to be accessible and transparent, fostering active community participation in shaping the future of Sutton.

Massachusetts is a heavily Democratic state, but Sutton tends to be quite independently minded. For example in 2008 when almost the entire state of Massachusetts voted for Obama, Sutton was one of the only towns which voted for McCain.

We repealed the alcohol sales tax, but voted not to reduce the overall sales tax.
2008 Election Results
The dog racing ban succeeded this year. Marijuana was decriminalized for small amounts (a fine, no jail time). An attempt to completely repeal the income tax was defeated.
2006 Election Results
Wine sales in food stores was defeated.
2004 Election Results
Worcester county wholeheartedly endored allowing marijuana use for medical reasons, in a non-binding ballot.
2002 Election Results
Romney came in as governor.
2000 Election Results
A dog racing ban failed. Voters DID vote to reduce state income tax from from 5.95% to 5%. However, the Mass legislature then ignored those results.

# Town Meeting & Election

The Town of Sutton is governed by General Bylaws, Home Rule Charter, Massachusetts General Law, and other relevant statutes. The Town's form of government, an elected, five-member Select Board appoints a Town Manager to administer the daily operation of the Town. The Town's legislative body is Open Town Meeting. According to the General Bylaws, the Town Manager must submit a balanced budget annually to the Select Board and Finance and Warrant Advisory Committee. The budget is reviewed by the Select Board before being moved to the Finance and Warrant Advisory Committee. The Finance and Warrant Advisory Committee reviews the annual operating budget and other warrant articles and submits their recommendations to Town Meeting. Town Meeting then votes to adopt the annual operating budget and other warrant articles at the Annual Town Meeting. Information related to the budget process, town meeting and the town election can be found below.

# Election

The 2026 election season includes two important statewide elections: the State Primary Election on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, and the State General Election on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. These elections determine who will represent Massachusetts at the federal, state, county, and local levels.

### State General Election – November 3, 2026

The General Election is when all registered voters cast their ballots to elect public officials. The ballot will include candidates for offices such as Governor, Lieutenant Governor, Attorney General, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Treasurer, Auditor, U.S. Senator, U.S. Representative, State Senator, State Representative, and other offices that may vary by community.

### Important Election Dates

  * State General Election: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
  * General Election Voter Registration Deadline: October 24, 2026
  * General Election Early Voting: October 17–30, 2026
  * General Election Vote-by-Mail Application Deadline: October 27, 2026

# Town Meeting

The Town of Sutton follows a traditional open town meeting process, which provides an important platform for residents to engage in local governance. Town meetings are typically held twice a year, in the spring (the 2nd Monday of May) and in the fall (the 3rd Monday of October). Voters gather to discuss and decide on key community issues, including budgets, zoning laws, and other local policies. In this forum, residents can propose, debate, and vote on a range of topics, ensuring that decisions reflect the collective voice of the town. The meeting is designed to be accessible and transparent, fostering active community participation in shaping the future of Sutton.

The declaration of the vote was as follows: ANNUAL TOWN ELECTION May 13, 2025 Pursuant to the warrant for the Annual Town Election, the polls were declared open by Mary Ellen Larsen, the Election Warden, at the Tisbury Emergency Services Facility at 215 Spring Street, on Tuesday May 13, 2025 at twelve noon. The ballot boxes were checked by the Election Warden and inspected by the Constable, Kenneth A. Barwick and found to be in order, with the registers set at zero at 11:30 a.m. The boxes were then locked by the Warden and the polls were declared open at twelve noon for the reception of votes. The polls were closed at 8:00 p.m. by the Warden with the ballot boxes registering 252 ballots cast. The checked voter's list and count of ballots showed 252 names checked and ballots counted. Kathleen M. Spofford, Town Clerk 
Phone:  978-597-1711 
 
 
 
Mission Statement  
The Town Clerk’s Office strives to be the heart of Town Hall; to serve the residents and 
general public in a helpful and friendly manner.  
 
Department Description  
The Town Clerk’s Office serves as the central information point for local residents and 
citizens at large.  The Town Clerk is the keeper for vital statistics, the custodian of the Town 
Seal, administers the oath of office to all persons elected or appointed to any Town office, 
and issues such licenses and permits as are permitted by law.  The Town Clerk supervises 
and manages the conduct of all elections and other matters relating to elections.  The Town 
Clerk serves as the Clerk of town meeting, keeps its records and in the absence of the Town 
Moderator and Deputy Moderator, presides pending election of a temporary Moderator by 
Town Meeting vote. The Town Clerk has such other powers and duties as given by the laws 
of the Commonwealth, the Town Charter, By-Laws and by other town Meeting vote.

# Town Clerk

### Town Clerk Responsibilities

The Truro Town Clerk's Office serves as the town's central administrative and record-keeping authority, fulfilling a broad range of essential functions for residents and all municipal bodies.

#### Key Responsibilities:

  * Official Record Keeper: The Town Clerk is the official custodian of all Town Meeting records and vital records (births, deaths, marriages) for Truro, dating back to the 1700s. 

  * Chief Election Official: As Truro's primary election authority, the Town Clerk manages every aspect of elections. This includes overseeing voter registration, absentee ballots, ballot preparation, polling place operations, and certifying nomination papers and results to the Secretary of State. The Clerk works in conjunction with the Board of Registrars to ensure fair and accurate elections.

  * Licensing and Permits: This office issues various state licenses and permits, such as marriage licenses, business certificates (DBAs), dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, and raffle/bazaar permits. 
Additionally, the Clerk is responsible for managing the annual census of town residents, a crucial task that helps maintain up-to-date demographic information for Truro, supporting various town services and planning initiatives.

  * Public Information & Liaison: The office serves as a primary point of contact, responding to inquiries from the public and collaborating with other town departments, boards, and committees. 

In essence, the Truro Town Clerk's Office acts as the custodian of the past and a vital link to the future, ensuring the smooth and transparent operation of local government for everyone in the community.

## Overview

### About Us

 The Town Clerk’s Office is responsible for: 

  * Serving as the Chief Election Official
  * Oversees polling places, election officers and the general conduct of all elections.
  * Directs preparations of ballots, polling places, voting equipment, voting lists, administers campaign finance laws, certifies nomination papers and initiative petitions, and serves on the Board of Registrars.
  * Supervises voter registration and absentee ballots and prepares, records, and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth.

 Other Responsibiltiies: 

  * Conducts the annual town census, prepares the street list of residents and school list, and furnishes the resident list to the Office of the Jury Commissioner.
  * Manages Vital Records including birth certificates, death certificate and marriage licenses.

 The Town Clerk meets with the public on Tuesdays from 11 am to 4 pm. 

 Forms can be picked up during regular Town Hall Hours -- and many can be downloaded from this website.

  * Licensing and Permits: This office issues various state licenses and permits, such as marriage licenses, business certificates (DBAs), dog licenses, fuel storage licenses, and raffle/bazaar permits. 
Additionally, the Clerk is responsible for managing the annual census of town residents, a crucial task that helps maintain up-to-date demographic information for Truro, supporting various town services and planning initiatives.

  * Public Information & Liaison: The office serves as a primary point of contact, responding to inquiries from the public and collaborating with other town departments, boards, and committees. 

In essence, the Truro Town Clerk's Office acts as the custodian of the past and a vital link to the future, ensuring the smooth and transparent operation of local government for everyone in the community.

## Overview

### About Us

 The Town Clerk’s Office is responsible for: 

  * Serving as the Chief Election Official
  * Oversees polling places, election officers and the general conduct of all elections.
  * Directs preparations of ballots, polling places, voting equipment, voting lists, administers campaign finance laws, certifies nomination papers and initiative petitions, and serves on the Board of Registrars.
  * Supervises voter registration and absentee ballots and prepares, records, and reports official election results to the Secretary of State of the Commonwealth.

 Other Responsibiltiies: 

  * Conducts the annual town census, prepares the street list of residents and school list, and furnishes the resident list to the Office of the Jury Commissioner.
  * Manages Vital Records including birth certificates, death certificate and marriage licenses.

 The Town Clerk meets with the public on Tuesdays from 11 am to 4 pm.

# Voting & Elections

## State Election: November 3, 2026

Wakefield residents vote at the Galvin Middle School, located at 525 Main Street.  Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

  * Precinct 4, 5, 6 sample ballot
  * Precinct 1, 2, 3, 7 sample ballot

The November 3, 2026 State Election ballot will include nine binding statewide ballot questions and one non-binding question for precincts 4, 5, and 6.. Detailed information on statewide ballot questions can be found on the state's website. 

### Early Voting Options

In-person early voting hours will take place at the Office of the Town Clerk in Town Hall, located at 1 Lafayette Street, during the following times:

  * Saturday, October 17 and Sunday, October 18, 2026: 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.
  * Saturday, October 24 and Sunday, October 25, 2026: 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.
  * Monday, October 19 through Friday, October 30, 2026: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

## Register to Vote

Residents can register to vote in three ways:

  * Online voter registration
  * Via mail using this form, returned to our Town Clerk's office
  * In person at our Town Clerk's office

## Absentee / Mail-in Ballots

Learn more about absentee and mail-in voting from the Secretary of the Commonwealth.

## Accessibility

Information specific for voters with disabilities is available from the Secretary of the Commonwealth. It includes types of equipment available, accessible voting procedures, and more.

# Town Clerk

### Welcome to the Office of the Town Clerk

Mission - The Town Clerk's Office is committed to providing accurate, efficient, and transparent services to the community. We maintain the town's official records, administer fair and secure elections, and provide public access to vital information and services in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.

Responsibilities - The Town Clerk serves as the town's Chief Election Official, overseeing voter registration, polling places, election officers, and the conduct of all elections. The office prepares ballots, maintains voting equipment and voter lists, administers campaign finance laws, certifies nomination papers and petitions, and serves on the Board of Registrars. The Town Clerk's Office also conducts the annual town census and prepares the town's street list of residents. As keeper of the town seal, the Town Clerk certifies official town documents including bylaws, contracts, bonds, and resolutions.

Records and Services - The Town Clerk's Office maintains and preserves the town's official records and archives. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The official results are in for Wayland's 2026 Annual Town Election. (Neal McNamara/Patch)

WAYLAND, MA — The official results are in for Wayland's 2026 Annual Town Election.

Wayland's Town Clerk said there were 795 votes cast, which represents 7.5 percent of the town's 10,613 registered voters.

Residents voted on the Select Board, Moderator, Board of Health, Planning Board, Recreation Commissioner, Board of Public Works, School Committee, Board of Assesors, Trustees of the Public Library, and Commissioner of Trust Funds.

Here's who won those official town positions:

# Green Burial

## Caring for your own at the time of death

With the interest in Green Burials and caring for our own in this town, we would like to share these guidelines on how to make the process as stress free as possible. The Wendell Cemetery Commission is sincerely committed to assisting you in a timely and respectful burial of your loved one When a funeral home is not involved, burial is time sensitive. It also leaves the family (who is coping with the loss of a loved one) with the legal documentation. Our Town Clerk can provide you with the necessary paperwork.

### If the death is anticipated

Plan ahead: have as many of the difficult conversations before death is imminent. Figure out who will complete each task because the family and friends are responsible for all plans and paperwork.

  1. Purchase a cemetery lot.
  2. Think about timing and which family members or friends will take on which tasks.

#### When death becomes imminent

  1. Notify the town clerk of pending death and complete initial paperwork.
  2. Notify cemetery commission.

#### At the time of death

  1. Contact the health care provider (a medical professional who has been treating the person) A hospice nurse can pronounce death. The doctor will complete death certificate.
  2. Contact town clerk and complete paperwork.
  3. The town clerk can then issue a permit to transport (formerly burial permit).
  4. Notify cemetery commission.
  5. The permit to transport and grave opening fee should be presented to the cemetery commission at the time of interment.

### If the death is not anticipated

  1. Call 911.
  2. The First responders will determine death and call the Medical Examiner.
  3. If the Medical examiner needs to examine the body a vehicle will be sent to pick it up. If it is not necessary the family should now notify the Town Clerk and Cemetery Commission as soon as possible.

Some funeral homes are now doing green burials but if the plan is to do it yourself the guidelines are the same with more details for green burial. A simple degradable box or shroud and a hole dug to four feet is usual.

Because feelings are deep and fragile at this time, it is important to have as much as possible done ahead of time. Have a check list and support system on hand to deal with the technical details.

Complete guidelines are available from the Funeral Consumers Alliance of Eastern Massachusetts.

## A few words from the Town Clerk re: Green Burials

If you are planning on a green burial or otherwise choosing not to use a Funeral Director please let people know so we can all help with the process. Communicate – speak with the Cemetery Commission and the Town Clerk. Both have folders of information that should answer FAQ. Make sure you know how to reach town contacts at home and at work.

When your loved one dies, alert the associated medical persons (Hospice or Primary Care) ASAP; don’t wait until the morning. Write down the time of death.

Assign 1 family member to speak with the Town Clerk and Cemetery Commissioner about what happens next.

Ask questions if things are not clear. Make sure everyone is on the same page.

When asked to complete a worksheet or sign a form, make sure the hand writing is legible. Except for your “signature”, print clearly and use black ink if possible.

The death certificate is intended to state where and when death occurred and cause of death. In addition, the person’s age, birth date, address, marital status, veteran status, occupation, birth place, parent’s names, doctor’s name, and burial information is included.

The Cemetery Commission is responsible for all things related to the burial.

The Town Clerk is responsible for all things related to the Electronic Death Registration System or EDRS. The end result of completing all the requested Forms and Worksheets is a completed Death Certificate. # Green Burial

## Caring for your own at the time of death

With the interest in Green Burials and caring for our own in this town, we would like to share these guidelines on how to make the process as stress free as possible. The Wendell Cemetery Commission is sincerely committed to assisting you in a timely and respectful burial of your loved one When a funeral home is not involved, burial is time sensitive. It also leaves the family (who is coping with the loss of a loved one) with the legal documentation. Our Town Clerk can provide you with the necessary paperwork.

### If the death is anticipated

Plan ahead: have as many of the difficult conversations before death is imminent. Figure out who will complete each task because the family and friends are responsible for all plans and paperwork.

  1. Purchase a cemetery lot.
  2. Think about timing and which family members or friends will take on which tasks.

#### When death becomes imminent

  1. Notify the town clerk of pending death and complete initial paperwork.
  2. Notify cemetery commission.

#### At the time of death

  1. Contact the health care provider (a medical professional who has been treating the person) A hospice nurse can pronounce death. The doctor will complete death certificate.
  2. Contact town clerk and complete paperwork.
  3. The town clerk can then issue a permit to transport (formerly burial permit).
  4. Notify cemetery commission.
  5. The permit to transport and grave opening fee should be presented to the cemetery commission at the time of interment.

### If the death is not anticipated

  1. Call 911.
  2. The First responders will determine death and call the Medical Examiner.
  3. If the Medical examiner needs to examine the body a vehicle will be sent to pick it up. If it is not necessary the family should now notify the Town Clerk and Cemetery Commission as soon as possible.

Some funeral homes are now doing green burials but if the plan is to do it yourself the guidelines are the same with more details for green burial. A simple degradable box or shroud and a hole dug to four feet is usual.

Because feelings are deep and fragile at this time, it is important to have as much as possible done ahead of time. Have a check list and support system on hand to deal with the technical details.

Complete guidelines are available from the Funeral Consumers Alliance of Eastern Massachusetts.

## A few words from the Town Clerk re: Green Burials

If you are planning on a green burial or otherwise choosing not to use a Funeral Director please let people know so we can all help with the process. Communicate – speak with the Cemetery Commission and the Town Clerk. Both have folders of information that should answer FAQ. Make sure you know how to reach town contacts at home and at work.

When your loved one dies, alert the associated medical persons (Hospice or Primary Care) ASAP; don’t wait until the morning. Write down the time of death.

Assign 1 family member to speak with the Town Clerk and Cemetery Commissioner about what happens next.

Ask questions if things are not clear. Make sure everyone is on the same page.

When asked to complete a worksheet or sign a form, make sure the hand writing is legible. Except for your “signature”, print clearly and use black ink if possible.

The death certificate is intended to state where and when death occurred and cause of death. In addition, the person’s age, birth date, address, marital status, veteran status, occupation, birth place, parent’s names, doctor’s name, and burial information is included.

The Cemetery Commission is responsible for all things related to the burial.

The Town Clerk is responsible for all things related to the Electronic Death Registration System or EDRS. The end result of completing all the requested Forms and Worksheets is a completed Death Certificate. You can expect to receive certified copies of the death certificate, as many copies as are needed by the family ($5/ea). An archival copy (special paper and ink) of the death certificate will become part of the permanent documents held in Wendell in the town vault. If at any time an additional copy of the death certificate is needed by the family, the Town Clerk can create a new certified copy from the permanent record. If in the future, the record cannot be found, the State will have the original and can mail you a copy for a fee. ## AN ACT CHANGING THE POSITION OF TOWN CLERK IN THE TOWN OF WENHAM FROM AN ELECTED POSITION TO AN APPOINTED POSITION

Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General Court assembled, and by the authority of the same, as follows:

SECTION 1. Notwithstanding any general or special law to the contrary, there shall be in the town of Wenham the position of appointed town clerk. The town clerk shall be appointed and may be removed by the select board and shall serve at the pleasure of the select board. The town clerk shall have all the powers and duties and be subject to the liabilities and penalties imposed by law on town clerks.

SECTION 2. This act shall be submitted to the voters of the town of Wenham at the next town election following the effective date of this act in the form of the following question that shall be placed on the official ballot:
          “Shall an act passed by the General Court entitled ‘An Act changing the position of town clerk in the town of Wenham from an elected position to an appointed position’ be accepted?”
          Below the question shall appear a summary of the act prepared by town counsel and approved by the select board. If a majority of the votes cast in answer to the question are in the affirmative, section 1 shall take effect in the town of Wenham, but not otherwise.

SECTION 3. Upon acceptance of this act by the voters of the town of Wenham, the elected office of town clerk shall be abolished and the term of the elected incumbent terminated; provided, however, that the elected incumbent holding the office of town clerk shall serve for a period of 5 months as the appointed town clerk, after which period appointments to the position of town clerk shall be made in accordance with section 1.

Approved, January 30, 2024.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

West Newbury, MA 01985 # Town Clerk ## Overview The Town Clerk’s Office is the official record keeper of the Town and serves as a central point of contact between residents and municipal government. Established under MGL Chapter 41, the Town Clerk is responsible for maintaining the Town’s vital records, official documents, bylaws, and meeting records, and for ensuring transparency, accountability, and public access to municipal information. The office of the Town Clerk is recognized as one of the oldest continuous public service positions in history, with roots that can be traced back to ancient Greece, where record keepers played a critical role in preserving laws and democratic processes.  The Town Clerk serves as the Town’s Chief Election Official, administering all local, state, and federal elections in accordance with Massachusetts election law, including voter registration, early voting, vote-by-mail, the annual town census, and the certification of election results. The office also supports Town Meeting and other public bodies by posting legal notices, attesting official actions, and maintaining permanent records. In addition, the Town Clerk’s Office administers licenses and permits as required by law, manages public records requests, and provides guidance to boards, committees, and the public on statutory procedures and compliance. West Brookfield

The results of the annual town election held on May 7 are as follows.

Catherine Lamica received 161 votes to secure a three-year term on the Board of Selectmen. Jonathan Bonin received 63 votes.

For the Planning Board, David Brown received 169 votes to secure a five-year term and 19 write-in candidates, Wesley Slobody received 13 votes for a one-year term.

The Board of Health had 21 write-in candidates, with Melvin Dorman receiving the majority of votes cast with three. There were 32 write-in candidates for the Housing Authority with Ann Toomey-Doane receiving the majority with 22.

For two three-year terms on the Quaboag Regional District School Committee, Craig Burgess received 153 votes, Bryan Griffing received 142 and Christine Luszcz received 139.

Jeffrey Robbins received 179 votes and David Swekla received 171 votes for two three-year terms on the Library Board of Trustees.

Klarissa Rose received 191 votes to serve as Town Clerk; Renee Adams-White received 186 votes to serve on the Board of Assessors; Diane Vayda received 187 votes to serve on the Common Committee; William Mansfield received 183 votes to serve as Moderator and Lester Paquette received 180 votes to serve as Water Commissioner.

# Town Clerk

## Mission

It is the mission of this office to be a reliable provider of information and quality services to the community and its residents, and to work cooperatively and in concert with all departments, boards and committees while complying with state and local statutes.

## Function

The Town Clerk's Office is the doorway to local government. The Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for residents and visitors alike. As the local arm of the Secretary of State's Office, the Town Clerk serves as the Public Information and Legislative Administrator, Chief Elections Officer and Local Registrar of Vital Records.

## Responsibilities

The Town Clerk's Office maintains the Town and Zoning Bylaws, the official town bulletin board, oaths of office, appointments and resignations of all Town Officials. The Town Clerk's Office issues state licenses and permits (including marriage licenses, business licenses and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses), and also processes requests for public documents.

The Town Clerk performs duties in accordance with the provisions of more than 73 Chapters and 451 sections of the Massachusetts General Laws. The Town Clerk serves as Registrar of Vital Statistics, Chief Election Officer, Clerk of the Board of Registrars, and the custodian of town records.

The Town Clerk is responsible for issuing marriage licenses and maintaining birth and death records.  The clerk also sells dog licenses as required by state law as well as hunting and fishing licenses. 

The Clerk coordinates and administers federal, state, and town elections. This includes ensuring that all statutory requirements are adhered to; supervising and training of all election officials; monitoring polling places to ensure conformance; administering absentee and early procedures; providing voting registration sessions; distributing and certifying nomination papers; recording results of election returns; maintaining the voter database; and maintaining and testing voting equipment.

Postings for all meetings for town boards and committees must be filed with the Clerk and posted per the Open Meeting Law. The Town Clerk is the Records Access Officer, who helps ensure access to public records in compliance with State Public Records Law and corresponding regulations.

# Town Clerk

## Mission

It is the mission of this office to be a reliable provider of information and quality services to the community and its residents, and to work cooperatively and in concert with all departments, boards and committees while complying with state and local statutes.

## Function

The Town Clerk's Office is the doorway to local government. The Town Clerk's Office serves as the central information point for residents and visitors alike. As the local arm of the Secretary of State's Office, the Town Clerk serves as the Public Information and Legislative Administrator, Chief Elections Officer and Local Registrar of Vital Records.

## Responsibilities

The Town Clerk's Office maintains the Town and Zoning Bylaws, the official town bulletin board, oaths of office, appointments and resignations of all Town Officials. The Town Clerk's Office issues state licenses and permits (including marriage licenses, business licenses and renewals, dog licenses, fuel storage licenses), and also processes requests for public documents.

The Town Clerk is the keeper of official records and handles many administrative tasks within the town government.

The Town Clerk is the municipality’s the chief election officer, overseeing all local, state, and national elections, and registering residents to vote. T he Town Clerk issues certified copies of birth, marriage, and death records, upon request, and issues Dog Licenses and Kennel Licenses.   The Clerk also receives “Doing Business As” Certificates “…from persons conducting business under a “d/b/a”.

To receive assistance with these or other matters, use the links below, or contact the Town Clerk.

#### General Town Meeting and Election Information

Annual Town Meeting takes place on the second Saturday in May according to the Town’s General Bylaws. If necessiity demands it, the Moderator has the authority to continue the town meeting to another date and time in the same fiscal year.

One must be a registered voter in Westhampton to vote at Town Meeting. It is recommended that you arrive at least 15 minutes prior to Town Meeting for a timely check in. 

State and local elections take place at the Town Hall, 1 South Road. You must be a registered voter in Westhampton to vote.

The Annual Town Election takes place on the first Saturday in June.  This year, polls are open from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

#### Why must we vote in person at Town Meeting?

We sometimes receive inquiries from residents about voting, and in particular whether it is possible to vote at town meeting by absentee ballot or by proxy.  Under state law, neither is permitted.

Town meetings are governed by Chapter 39 of the Massachusetts General Laws.   The statute requires that voters be present at the meeting to hear the debate and exercise their right to vote.   Fun fact:  in colonial times attendance at town meeting was mandatory, and those who were absent or arrived late could be fined.

As a practical matter, absentee ballots at town meeting could not be effective as they are for elections.  In an election, the candidates and any referendum questions are known well in advance of the date.  At town meeting, on the other hand, no one can predict with certainty what motions or amendments may be proposed on town meeting floor.  It would be impossible to anticipate the questions to be decided in preparing an absentee ballot.

While some might be frustrated where their travel plans or other circumstances may prevent their attending in person.  However, the Town has no choice but to follow the requirements of state law.

# Here are the official results of Westford’s 2026 Annual Town Election

  * May 6, 2026
  * - By Alex Svenson

Image: Here are the official results of Westford’s 2026 Annual Town Election

WESTFORD CENTER – Several key races were on the ballot during Westford’s annual town election on Tuesday, May 5.

Polls opened at 7 a.m. and stayed open until 8 p.m. Voting took place at two locations. Residents in precincts One, Three, Four and Seven cast their ballots at Westford Academy, while voters in precincts Two, Five and Six headed to the Stony Brook School.

Voters had the opportunity to cast ballots on multiple open seats on the Select Board. Two three-year positions were contested, with a separate one-year Select Board seat available, which was added to the ballot following the resignation announcement of Select Board Clerk John Cunningham earlier this year.

In the Select Board race for three-year term seats, incumbent Chris Barrett led the field with 1,432 votes, followed by Tom Clay with 1,352 votes. Both secured the available seats. Challenger Meghan O’Connell received 655 votes, finishing well behind the incumbents in a race that saw a combined total of nearly 4,000 ballots cast.

Meanwhile, in the Select Board race for a single available one-year term seat, Elizabeth Sawyer won convincingly with 1,179 votes. She more than doubled the total of runner-up Scott Hazelton, who received 544 votes, while David Pina trailed with 205.

The Board of Health race saw Maeghan Hughes receive 1,493 votes while Naseem Chatiwala got 1,412. Both will fill the two available three-year seats.

For Library Trustees, two three-year term seats were on the ballot. Mary Siegel received 1,493 votes while Dana Riegert earned 1,485 votes.

The School Committee race also featured two three-year term seats. Valery Young, who currently serves as Committee Vice Chair, received 1,532 votes, while William McDonald, also a current Committee member, racked up 1,487. Both candidates secured the available three-year seats with strong support across all precincts.

The Town Clerk is the keeper of official records and handles many administrative tasks within the town government.

The Town Clerk is the municipality’s the chief election officer, overseeing all local, state, and national elections, and registering residents to vote. #### General Town Meeting and Election Information

Annual Town Meeting takes place on the second Saturday in May according to the Town’s General Bylaws. If necessiity demands it, the Moderator has the authority to continue the town meeting to another date and time in the same fiscal year.

One must be a registered voter in Westhampton to vote at Town Meeting. It is recommended that you arrive at least 15 minutes prior to Town Meeting for a timely check in. 

State and local elections take place at the Town Hall, 1 South Road. You must be a registered voter in Westhampton to vote.

The Annual Town Election takes place on the first Saturday in June.  This year, polls are open from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

#### Why must we vote in person at Town Meeting?

We sometimes receive inquiries from residents about voting, and in particular whether it is possible to vote at town meeting by absentee ballot or by proxy.  Under state law, neither is permitted.

Town meetings are governed by Chapter 39 of the Massachusetts General Laws.   The statute requires that voters be present at the meeting to hear the debate and exercise their right to vote.   Fun fact:  in colonial times attendance at town meeting was mandatory, and those who were absent or arrived late could be fined.

As a practical matter, absentee ballots at town meeting could not be effective as they are for elections.  In an election, the candidates and any referendum questions are known well in advance of the date.  At town meeting, on the other hand, no one can predict with certainty what motions or amendments may be proposed on town meeting floor.  It would be impossible to anticipate the questions to be decided in preparing an absentee ballot.

While some might be frustrated where their travel plans or other circumstances may prevent their attending in person.  However, the Town has no choice but to follow the requirements of state law.

# Here are the official results of Westford’s 2026 Annual Town Election

  * May 6, 2026
  * - By Alex Svenson

Image: Here are the official results of Westford’s 2026 Annual Town Election

WESTFORD CENTER – Several key races were on the ballot during Westford’s annual town election on Tuesday, May 5.

Polls opened at 7 a.m. and stayed open until 8 p.m. Voting took place at two locations. Residents in precincts One, Three, Four and Seven cast their ballots at Westford Academy, while voters in precincts Two, Five and Six headed to the Stony Brook School.

Voters had the opportunity to cast ballots on multiple open seats on the Select Board. Two three-year positions were contested, with a separate one-year Select Board seat available, which was added to the ballot following the resignation announcement of Select Board Clerk John Cunningham earlier this year.

In the Select Board race for three-year term seats, incumbent Chris Barrett led the field with 1,432 votes, followed by Tom Clay with 1,352 votes. Both secured the available seats. Challenger Meghan O’Connell received 655 votes, finishing well behind the incumbents in a race that saw a combined total of nearly 4,000 ballots cast.

Meanwhile, in the Select Board race for a single available one-year term seat, Elizabeth Sawyer won convincingly with 1,179 votes. She more than doubled the total of runner-up Scott Hazelton, who received 544 votes, while David Pina trailed with 205.

The Board of Health race saw Maeghan Hughes receive 1,493 votes while Naseem Chatiwala got 1,412. Both will fill the two available three-year seats.

For Library Trustees, two three-year term seats were on the ballot. Mary Siegel received 1,493 votes while Dana Riegert earned 1,485 votes.

The School Committee race also featured two three-year term seats. Valery Young, who currently serves as Committee Vice Chair, received 1,532 votes, while William McDonald, also a current Committee member, racked up 1,487. Both candidates secured the available three-year seats with strong support across all precincts.
